kerberoastable-hash-es-captured-aada6591.title: Kerberoastable service account(s)
kerberoastable-hash-es-captured-aada6591.why: Any domain user can request a Kerberos service ticket (TGS) for an account with an SPN; the ticket is encrypted with the account's NTLM hash and can be cracked offline. Weak service-account passwords yield domain credentials.

fix.label: Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA)
fix.text: Replace SPN-bearing user accounts with gMSAs so Windows manages a 120-char random password that rotates automatically.

fix.label: Enforce strong passwords where gMSA is impossible
fix.text: Set service-account passwords to >=25 random characters and audit SPN accounts with `Get-ADUser -Filter {ServicePrincipalName -like '*'}`.

as-rep-roastable-hash-es-captured-5c4e28.title: AS-REP roastable account(s) (no pre-auth)
as-rep-roastable-hash-es-captured-5c4e28.why: Accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' let any unauthenticated attacker request an AS-REP encrypted with the account's key, crackable offline.

fix.label: Re-enable Kerberos pre-authentication
fix.text: Clear 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' (DONT_REQ_PREAUTH) on every account; it is rarely required.

bunconstrained-delegation-b-d66ecf6e.title: Unconstrained Kerberos delegation
bunconstrained-delegation-b-d66ecf6e.why: A host trusted for unconstrained delegation caches the TGTs of every user who authenticates to it. Compromising it (or coercing a DC to authenticate to it) yields a DC TGT and full domain compromise.

fix.label: Remove unconstrained delegation
fix.text: Switch to constrained delegation or resource-based constrained delegation; never leave non-DC hosts TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION.

fix.label: Protect sensitive accounts
fix.text: Mark privileged accounts 'Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated' and add them to Protected Users.

bmsds-allowedtoactonbehalfofotheridentit.title: Resource-based constrained delegation writable (RBCD)
bmsds-allowedtoactonbehalfofotheridentit.why: msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity on a computer object lets the named principal impersonate any user to that host. If writable (or the attacker can add a computer via MachineAccountQuota), it is a direct takeover primitive.

fix.label: Restrict write access to computer objects
fix.text: Audit and remove non-admin write/GenericWrite on computer objects; clear unexpected msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity values.

fix.label: Set MachineAccountQuota to 0
fix.text: Prevents low-priv users creating the computer account RBCD abuse needs.

bms-ds-machineaccountquota-d-d534b185.title: ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota > 0
bms-ds-machineaccountquota-d-d534b185.why: The default MachineAccountQuota of 10 lets any authenticated user create computer accounts, a precondition for RBCD, noPac, and other privilege-escalation chains.

fix.label: Set quota to 0
fix.text: Set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota=0 on the domain head and delegate machine creation to a dedicated group only.

esc-1-9-1-0-6-s-vulnerable-a432e7de.title: AD CS template vulnerable (ESC1–ESC16)
esc-1-9-1-0-6-s-vulnerable-a432e7de.why: A misconfigured certificate template (enrollee-supplies-subject, EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2, vulnerable enrollment agent, etc.) lets a low-priv user enroll a cert that authenticates as any user including Domain Admins.

fix.label: Remediate per ESC class
fix.text: Remove enrollee-supplies-subject on auth templates, disable EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 on the CA, restrict enrollment rights, and enable manager approval for sensitive templates.

fix.label: Enforce strong certificate mapping
fix.text: Apply the May 2022 KB5014754 certificate-mapping enforcement so SANs cannot be forged.

besc8-relay-target-b-e9ab15ea.title: AD CS ESC8 — HTTP enrollment relay target
besc8-relay-target-b-e9ab15ea.why: The CA web-enrollment endpoint accepts NTLM over HTTP, so a coerced DC authentication can be relayed to it to obtain a DC certificate — full domain compromise.

fix.label: Enforce HTTPS + EPA / channel binding
fix.text: Require HTTPS and Extended Protection for Authentication on the certsrv site, or disable web enrollment; enable RPC/LDAP signing and disable NTLM to the CA.

gpp-cpassword-in-36f4a9ed.title: GPP cpassword in SYSVOL (MS14-025)
gpp-cpassword-in-36f4a9ed.why: Group Policy Preferences stored a password encrypted with a Microsoft-published AES key in SYSVOL, readable by every domain user and trivially decrypted.

fix.label: Remove the GPP password and rotate it
fix.text: Delete the offending Groups.xml/Services.xml/etc. from SYSVOL, change the exposed account's password, and never store credentials in GPP (use LAPS/gMSA).

bcpassword-s-s-e9039ab6.title: cpassword value exposed
bcpassword-s-s-e9039ab6.why: A GPP cpassword attribute was found. It is AES-encrypted with a public key and decrypts to a cleartext credential usable across the domain.

fix.label: Rotate and purge
fix.text: Rotate the exposed credential immediately and remove the cpassword-bearing GPP from SYSVOL.

readable-lapsv-12-d043180c.title: LAPS password readable
readable-lapsv-12-d043180c.why: The Local Administrator Password Solution password is readable by the enumerating principal, exposing the local admin password of the managed computer.

fix.label: Restrict LAPS read rights
fix.text: Audit ms-Mcs-AdmPwd / msLAPS-Password read permissions; grant only to tier-0 admins, and remove inherited 'All extended rights' from non-admins.

encrypted-lapsv2-2540a156.title: LAPS v2 encrypted password present
encrypted-lapsv2-2540a156.why: Windows LAPS v2 stores the managed password encrypted; its presence confirms LAPS is deployed. If the enumerating principal can decrypt it, the local admin password is exposed.

fix.label: Restrict decryption rights
fix.text: Ensure only tier-0 principals hold the LAPS encryption/read rights; prefer AES-256 DPAPI-NG encryption scoped to a dedicated group.

blaps-d-computer-object-s-expose-b-e3bda.title: LAPS passwords exposed across computer objects
blaps-d-computer-object-s-expose-b-e3bda.why: Multiple computer objects expose their LAPS-managed local-admin password to the enumerating principal — a broad local-admin credential harvest.

fix.label: Re-scope LAPS read rights
fix.text: Remove non-admin read access to ms-Mcs-AdmPwd / msLAPS-Password across all OUs; grant per-OU to tier-appropriate admins only.

printnightmare-configuration-is-exploita.title: PrintNightmare exploitable (CVE-2021-34527)
printnightmare-configuration-is-exploita.why: The Print Spooler configuration permits non-admin driver installation / point-and-print, allowing remote code execution as SYSTEM on the host, including domain controllers.

fix.label: Patch and harden point-and-print
fix.text: Apply the CVE-2021-34527 updates, set RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators=1, and disable the Print Spooler on servers that do not print (especially DCs).

petitpotam-coerce-chain-available-f4420e.title: PetitPotam coercion chain available
petitpotam-coerce-chain-available-f4420e.why: MS-EFSRPC lets an attacker coerce a DC/host to authenticate to an attacker machine, which can be relayed (e.g. to AD CS ESC8) for domain compromise.

fix.label: Block the coercion + relay
fix.text: Apply PetitPotam patches, enable SMB/LDAP signing and EPA, disable NTLM where possible, and filter the MS-EFSRPC named pipes.

bwebclient-service-running-coercion-b-3b.title: WebClient service running (coercion via WebDAV)
bwebclient-service-running-coercion-b-3b.why: The WebClient service enables WebDAV coercion (e.g. via PetitPotam/PrinterBug over HTTP), which can be relayed to AD CS or LDAP for privilege escalation.

fix.label: Disable WebClient where unneeded
fix.text: Disable the WebClient service via GPO on servers/workstations that do not require WebDAV, and enable EPA on relay targets.

lsarpc-anonymous-reachable-on-dc-4e8a424.title: LSARPC anonymous access on a DC
lsarpc-anonymous-reachable-on-dc-4e8a424.why: Anonymous LSARPC access leaks domain SIDs, policy, and user/group names, aiding targeted attacks and confirming weak null-session restrictions on a domain controller.

fix.label: Restrict anonymous access
fix.text: Set 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' and RestrictRemoteSam; audit Everyone/Anonymous in Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access.

bmsrpc-anonymous-srvinfo-33223179.title: MSRPC anonymous srvinfo disclosure
bmsrpc-anonymous-srvinfo-33223179.why: Anonymous MSRPC srvinfo leaks the host OS/version and server role, useful for fingerprinting and null-session enumeration.

fix.label: Restrict anonymous RPC
fix.text: Apply RestrictRemoteSam / RestrictAnonymous and remove Anonymous Logon from pre-Windows-2000 compatibility groups.

btrust-auth-b-920e530b.title: PostgreSQL/host TRUST authentication
btrust-auth-b-920e530b.why: A TRUST auth method accepts connections with no password for the matching host, granting the database/service account without credentials.

fix.label: Replace trust with scram-sha-256
fix.text: Edit pg_hba.conf: change `trust` to `scram-sha-256`, restrict host CIDRs, and reload. Never use `trust` outside localhost sockets.

badmin-admin-works-b-479f083c.title: Default credential admin:admin accepted
badmin-admin-works-b-479f083c.why: The service accepts admin:admin, granting administrative access with a trivially guessed default.

fix.label: Change the default credential
fix.text: Set a unique strong password, disable or rename the default admin account, and enforce an account-lockout policy.

bguest-guest-b-34b991e6.title: Guest account enabled / guest:guest
bguest-guest-b-34b991e6.why: The guest account is enabled and accepts guest:guest, exposing anonymous-equivalent access and SMB enumeration.

fix.label: Disable the Guest account
fix.text: Disable Guest via GPO ('Accounts: Guest account status' = Disabled) and deny guest network logon.

bsigning-disabled-b-bsigning-enabled-but.title: SMB signing not required (NTLM relay)
bsigning-disabled-b-bsigning-enabled-but.why: SMB signing is disabled or not enforced, so captured/coerced NTLM authentication can be relayed to this host for code execution or privilege escalation.

fix.label: Require SMB signing (GPO)
fix.text: Set 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' = Enabled on servers and clients.

blocalaccounttokenfilterpolicy-1-b-deda8.title: LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy=1 (remote local-admin)
blocalaccounttokenfilterpolicy-1-b-deda8.why: This setting disables UAC remote restrictions, so any local administrator account can authenticate remotely with a full high-integrity token — ideal for lateral movement with reused local creds.

fix.label: Set it back to 0
fix.text: Remove or set LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy=0 via GPO; deploy LAPS so local-admin passwords are unique per host.

bwdigest-uselogoncredential-1-b-909bd9e4.title: WDigest UseLogonCredential=1 (cleartext in LSASS)
bwdigest-uselogoncredential-1-b-909bd9e4.why: With UseLogonCredential=1, WDigest caches cleartext passwords in LSASS, so an LSASS dump yields plaintext domain credentials.

fix.label: Set UseLogonCredential=0
fix.text: Set it to 0 via GPO, enable Credential Guard, and add privileged users to Protected Users.

bnetbios-workgroup-mismatch-high-value-b.title: NetBIOS workgroup mismatch (high value)
bnetbios-workgroup-mismatch-high-value-b.why: A host advertises a workgroup/domain name inconsistent with the environment, often indicating a rogue, unmanaged, or legacy system worth targeting.

fix.label: Investigate and bring under management
fix.text: Identify the host owner, join it to the correct domain or decommission it, and ensure it is covered by patch/EDR baselines.

bbloodhound-collection-e26e0ea7.title: BloodHound collection succeeded
bbloodhound-collection-e26e0ea7.why: A full BloodHound graph was collected, meaning an authenticated user can map every attack path to Domain Admins — the data an attacker uses to plan privilege escalation.

fix.label: Remediate the shortest paths
fix.text: Import the graph, run the pre-built 'shortest paths to Domain Admins' queries, and remove the risky edges (excess ACLs, stale admin rights, delegation).

bloodhound-zip-b0e51d91.title: BloodHound data archive produced
bloodhound-zip-b0e51d91.why: A BloodHound ZIP of collected domain data exists; it contains the full attack-path graph and should be treated as sensitive.

fix.label: Act on the graph and protect it
fix.text: Use the graph to remediate attack paths, then store/destroy the archive securely — it maps your domain for an attacker.

member-of-domain-admins-enterprise-admin.title: Principal in a tier-0 privileged group
member-of-domain-admins-enterprise-admin.why: The assessed principal is a member of a domain-dominant group (Domain/Enterprise/Schema Admins, Administrators, Backup/Server Operators, Hyper-V Admins) — effective domain compromise if that principal is obtainable.

fix.label: Reduce tier-0 membership
fix.text: Remove standing membership, use time-bound PIM/JIT elevation, and enforce tiered administration so day-to-day accounts are never tier-0.

member-of-account-operators-print-operat.title: Principal in a privilege-escalation group
member-of-account-operators-print-operat.why: Account Operators, Print Operators, and DnsAdmins each have documented paths to domain compromise (e.g. DnsAdmins DLL injection into the DNS service running as SYSTEM on a DC).

fix.label: Empty or tightly control these groups
fix.text: Remove unnecessary members; treat DnsAdmins/Account Operators/Print Operators as tier-0-adjacent and monitor changes.

member-of-remote-desktop-users-remote-ma.title: Principal in a remote-access group
member-of-remote-desktop-users-remote-ma.why: Remote Desktop Users / Remote Management Users grants interactive or WinRM access to hosts, enabling lateral movement and credential harvesting from those sessions.

fix.label: Restrict remote-access groups
fix.text: Limit membership to required admins, require MFA/network-level authentication for RDP, and segment management access.

badfs-sign-on-page-detected-b-120f5ed6.title: ADFS sign-on page detected
badfs-sign-on-page-detected-b-120f5ed6.why: An exposed ADFS endpoint is a high-value target for password spraying and, if misconfigured, token forgery (Golden SAML) affecting federated cloud access.

fix.label: Harden ADFS
fix.text: Require Extranet Smart Lockout/MFA, disable IdP-initiated sign-on if unused, protect the token-signing key, and monitor for Golden SAML indicators.

bexchange-endpoint-detected-b-b3d82fbe.title: Exchange endpoint detected
bexchange-endpoint-detected-b-b3d82fbe.why: On-prem Exchange (OWA/ECP/Autodiscover/EWS) is a recurring RCE/SSRF target (ProxyLogon, ProxyShell) and a password-spray surface tied to AD identities.

fix.label: Patch and reduce exposure
fix.text: Apply the latest Exchange CU+SU, run the Exchange Health Checker, restrict ECP/management to internal networks, and enable Extended Protection.

bsccm-client-present-b-06b233a7.title: SCCM/MECM client present
bsccm-client-present-b-06b233a7.why: SCCM/MECM is a high-value lateral-movement and credential surface (Network Access Accounts, PXE, application deployment to many hosts).

fix.label: Harden SCCM
fix.text: Remove legacy Network Access Accounts (use Enhanced HTTP), require PXE passwords, enable site-system PKI, and restrict who can deploy applications.

bwsus-over-http-69eee442.title: WSUS served over HTTP
bwsus-over-http-69eee442.why: WSUS over cleartext HTTP allows a man-in-the-middle to inject a malicious signed-wrapper update and achieve SYSTEM-level code execution on clients.

fix.label: Require HTTPS for WSUS
fix.text: Reconfigure WSUS and the client GPO to use HTTPS (8531), or isolate the update path; consider SpecOps/third-party TLS enforcement.

ccm-logs-passwordhash-naa-credential-184.title: SCCM Network Access Account credential in CCM logs
ccm-logs-passwordhash-naa-credential-184.why: The SCCM client logs/policy expose a Network Access Account credential (PasswordHash/NAA), a reusable domain credential recoverable by any local user on the client.

fix.label: Rotate and remove NAA
fix.text: Rotate the NAA credential, migrate to Enhanced HTTP / PKI so no NAA is needed, and clear the exposed logs/policy.

all-s-s-all-s-all-46200da3.title: Unrestricted sudo access
all-s-s-all-s-all-46200da3.why: A sudoers rule granting (ALL:ALL) ALL allows the affected user to execute any command as any user or group. This is effectively full root access, so defenders must verify that the grant is intentional and tightly controlled.

fix.label: Apply least privilege
fix.text: Replace the unrestricted rule with an explicit allowlist of required commands, target users, and groups; remove the rule entirely if it is unnecessary.

alwaysinstallelevated-enabled-6495dbaa.title: AlwaysInstallElevated enabled
alwaysinstallelevated-enabled-6495dbaa.why: When AlwaysInstallElevated is enabled in both the machine and user policy hives, Windows Installer packages can run with elevated privileges. A local user may therefore obtain SYSTEM-level execution by launching a malicious MSI package.

b-release-agent-notify-on-release-core-p.title: Writable kernel control interface
b-release-agent-notify-on-release-core-p.why: A non-root user can write a sensitive kernel or cgroup control such as release_agent, notify_on_release, core_pattern, or sysrq-trigger. Depending on the interface and surrounding isolation, this can alter privileged execution behavior, expose host control, or destabilize the system.

fix.label: Restrict ownership and writes
fix.text: Make the control root-owned and remove write access from untrusted users; also prevent sensitive host procfs, sysfs, and cgroup paths from being mounted writable inside containers.

bcap-net-raw-net-bind-service-kill-sys-r.title: Executable has elevated Linux capabilities
bcap-net-raw-net-bind-service-kill-sys-r.why: The executable carries an effective capability such as raw networking, privileged-port binding, process signaling, or raw device I/O. If the program is unnecessary, writable, or can invoke user-controlled behavior, that capability may enable traffic manipulation, service impersonation, process interference, or hardware access.

fix.label: Constrain required capability use
fix.text: If the capability is required, use a narrowly scoped service account, protect the executable and its dependencies from modification, and restrict execution to authorized users.

bcap-setuid-setgid-dac-read-search-dac-o.title: Executable has high-impact capabilities
bcap-setuid-setgid-dac-read-search-dac-o.why: The executable has an effective capability that can bypass file permissions, alter identities, trace processes, load modules, administer the system, or access raw devices. A flaw or user-controlled execution path in that binary can turn the delegated capability into local privilege escalation or sensitive-data access.

fix.label: Replace broad delegation
fix.text: Use a dedicated privileged service or a minimal capability set instead of granting broad capabilities to a general-purpose executable.

bcap-setuid-setgid-dac-read-search-dac-o.title: Dangerous effective file capability
bcap-setuid-setgid-dac-read-search-dac-o.why: An executable is effective with a powerful capability covering identity changes, discretionary-access bypass, system administration, tracing, module loading, ownership changes, or network administration. These privileges can cross important security boundaries and should not be attached to general-purpose or user-modifiable programs.

fix.label: Redesign privileged operation
fix.text: Delegate only the minimum required operation through a protected service, and ensure the executable, libraries, configuration, and parent directories are not writable by untrusted users.

bcap-sys-admin-held-b-blooks-privileged-.title: Container holds broad host capability
bcap-sys-admin-held-b-blooks-privileged-.why: CAP_SYS_ADMIN is an exceptionally broad capability associated with mounts, namespaces, and many kernel administration operations; a privileged container commonly holds still more authority. If the container is compromised, weak isolation or exposed host resources can make host compromise substantially easier.

fix.label: Drop broad capabilities
fix.text: Run the workload without privileged mode, drop all capabilities by default, and add back only capabilities proven necessary; never grant CAP_SYS_ADMIN unless the workload is fully trusted.

bdocker-sock-present-b-01283762.title: Docker control socket exposed
bdocker-sock-present-b-01283762.why: Access to the Docker daemon socket permits control of containers and commonly provides a path to host-level root authority. Exposing the socket inside a workload turns compromise of that workload into compromise of the container-management plane.

fix.label: Remove socket exposure
fix.text: Do not mount the Docker socket into containers. Where management access is unavoidable, use a narrowly authorized proxy and restrict socket membership to trusted administrators.

bno-all-squash-b-862fbcde.title: NFS export preserves client identities
bno-all-squash-b-862fbcde.why: An NFS export using no_all_squash preserves client-supplied user identities rather than mapping every request to an anonymous account. In environments without strong NFS authentication, matching or spoofed numeric UIDs can grant unintended access to exported data.

fix.label: Map untrusted clients
fix.text: Use all_squash with a dedicated anonymous UID/GID for untrusted clients, restrict each export to necessary client networks, and use Kerberos-secured NFS where identity assurance is required.

bno-root-squash-b-b4bfb72e.title: NFS root squashing disabled
bno-root-squash-b-b4bfb72e.why: An NFS export with no_root_squash accepts client root as root on the exported filesystem. A compromised or attacker-controlled authorized client can create root-owned files, alter executable content, or plant privileged configuration consumed by the server.

fix.label: Enable root squashing
fix.text: Remove no_root_squash or explicitly use root_squash, restrict the export to required clients, and reload the export table with exportfs -ra.

bpossible-host-pid-namespace-b-dbd24c2f.title: Possible host PID namespace sharing
bpossible-host-pid-namespace-b-dbd24c2f.why: A container that shares the host PID namespace can enumerate and potentially interact with host processes subject to its capabilities and other controls. This weakens process isolation and can expose command lines, environment data, signals, or debugging interfaces.

fix.label: Restore PID isolation
fix.text: Disable host PID sharing for the workload, retain the runtime's private PID namespace, and drop process-control capabilities such as SYS_PTRACE and KILL unless explicitly required.

bse-backup-restore-takeownership-managev.title: High-impact Windows privilege enabled
bse-backup-restore-takeownership-managev.why: The current token has an enabled privilege capable of bypassing file ACLs, restoring protected content, taking ownership, managing volumes, or accessing security auditing functions. Abuse can expose protected credentials or let a compromised process alter security-sensitive resources.

fix.label: Restrict user-right assignments
fix.text: Remove the account from the corresponding User Rights Assignment unless operationally required, and run backup, restore, storage, and security-management duties through dedicated, monitored service accounts.

bse-impersonate-assignprimarytoken-debug.title: Dangerous Windows privilege assigned
bse-impersonate-assignprimarytoken-debug.why: A sensitive privilege is present in the process token but currently disabled. Windows may enable an assigned privilege when an authorized operation requests it, so assignment still expands the impact of process compromise and warrants least-privilege review.

fix.label: Remove unnecessary assignments
fix.text: Use Local Security Policy or Group Policy to remove unneeded sensitive user rights from the account and its groups; separate administrative duties into dedicated identities.

bse-impersonate-assignprimarytoken-debug.title: Critical Windows privilege enabled
bse-impersonate-assignprimarytoken-debug.why: The current token has an enabled privilege permitting impersonation, primary-token assignment, debugging, trusted-computing-base behavior, token creation, or driver loading. These rights can cross user and kernel trust boundaries and frequently make compromise of the process equivalent to full system compromise.

fix.label: Remove sensitive user rights
fix.text: Remove the affected rights from ordinary users and services through Group Policy, use dedicated service identities, and grant only the specific right required by the application.

bwritable-b-etc-cron-78249dc5.title: Writable system cron configuration
bwritable-b-etc-cron-78249dc5.why: An untrusted user can modify a system cron file or directory whose jobs may execute as root or another privileged account. Injected commands would then run automatically under that job's security context.

bwritable-b-etc-systemd-f4b4a67c.title: Writable systemd configuration
bwritable-b-etc-systemd-f4b4a67c.why: An untrusted user can modify a systemd unit, override, or related configuration under /etc/systemd. If a privileged unit is started, restarted, or reloaded, attacker-controlled directives may execute with that unit's privileges.

fix.label: Review unit integrity
fix.text: Compare the unit and all drop-ins with trusted package or configuration-management sources, then run systemctl daemon-reload after correcting them.

docker-sock-ca319bcd.title: Docker socket accessible
docker-sock-ca319bcd.why: The Docker API socket is present in the assessed environment. Any user or workload able to access it can often create or alter containers with host mounts and elevated settings, effectively obtaining host-level control.

fix.label: Limit daemon access
fix.text: Remove the socket from containers, restrict membership in the docker group to trusted administrators, and use an authorization proxy when applications require limited API access.

env-keep-ld-preload-library-path-f389f6e.title: Sudo preserves dynamic-loader variables
env-keep-ld-preload-library-path-f389f6e.why: A sudoers env_keep rule preserves LD_PRELOAD or LD_LIBRARY_PATH across a privilege boundary. When the invoked program honors these variables, user-selected libraries may be loaded into a privileged process and execute with elevated rights.

fix.label: Remove loader variables
fix.text: Delete LD_PRELOAD and LD_LIBRARY_PATH from sudoers env_keep entries, retain env_reset, and validate the resulting policy with visudo -c.

etc-apt-sources-list-writable-3e435145.title: Writable APT repository configuration
etc-apt-sources-list-writable-3e435145.why: An untrusted user can alter an APT source definition and redirect package retrieval to an attacker-controlled repository. A later privileged update or installation could introduce untrusted software, especially where repository-signing controls are weak or misconfigured.

fix.label: Verify repository trust
fix.text: Review configured repository URLs and signing-key scopes, remove unknown entries, and use Signed-By with a dedicated keyring for each external repository.

etc-usr-lib-lib64-sbin-bin-s-s-s-world-w.title: World-writable system path
etc-usr-lib-lib64-sbin-bin-s-s-s-world-w.why: A file or directory beneath a trusted system path is writable by every local user. Attackers may replace executables, libraries, configuration, or scripts that privileged users and services rely upon, creating a durable privilege-escalation path.

fix.label: Restore trusted ownership
fix.text: Set ownership to the package- or service-appropriate administrative account and verify the file against the operating-system package database or a trusted baseline.

glibc-s-s-s-in-vulnerable-window-s-2-34-.title: Potential Looney Tunables exposure
glibc-s-s-s-in-vulnerable-window-s-2-34-.why: The detected glibc release falls in the upstream version range associated with CVE-2023-4911, an ld.so environment-variable parsing flaw that can permit local privilege escalation through set-user-ID programs. Distribution packages may contain backported fixes, so the vendor package revision must be checked rather than relying only on the upstream version.

fix.label: Install vendor-fixed glibc
fix.text: Apply the distribution's security update for CVE-2023-4911 and restart affected long-running services or reboot according to vendor guidance.

groups-services-scheduledtasks-datasourc.title: Group Policy Preferences file exposed
groups-services-scheduledtasks-datasourc.why: A legacy Group Policy Preferences XML file was found in SYSVOL or a local policy cache. Such files can disclose account names and configuration details, and older entries containing cpassword values expose reversibly encrypted credentials to any domain user who can read SYSVOL.

fix.label: Remove embedded credentials
fix.text: Delete legacy cpassword-bearing preference items, rotate every referenced credential, purge stale copies from SYSVOL, and deploy managed service accounts or LAPS instead.

hardening-ptrace-scope-0-unprivileged-bp.title: Weak Linux kernel hardening setting
hardening-ptrace-scope-0-unprivileged-bp.why: One or more kernel controls permit broad process tracing, unprivileged BPF use, or dumpable privileged processes. These settings enlarge the local attack surface and can expose process memory, kernel interfaces, or sensitive crash data after another foothold is obtained.

fix.label: Apply hardened sysctl values
fix.text: Set kernel.yama.ptrace_scope to at least 1, kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled to the vendor-recommended restrictive value, and fs.suid_dumpable to 0 unless a documented operational need exists.

io-uring-reachable-to-current-user-s-s-k.title: io_uring available to unprivileged users
io-uring-reachable-to-current-user-s-s-k.why: The current unprivileged user can reach the io_uring kernel subsystem, which has historically contained several locally exploitable memory-safety flaws. Availability is not proof of a vulnerability, but it increases kernel attack surface and should be restricted where applications do not require it.

fix.label: Disable unused io_uring
fix.text: Patch to the vendor-supported kernel and set kernel.io_uring_disabled=2 when io_uring is not required, or use the supported restrictive mode and authorized group where available.

kernel-s-s-s-in-ubuntu-hwe-cve-2023-0386.title: Ubuntu kernel vulnerable to CVE-2023-0386
kernel-s-s-s-in-ubuntu-hwe-cve-2023-0386.why: The detected Ubuntu HWE kernel appears to fall within the vulnerable range for CVE-2023-0386, an OverlayFS flaw that can allow a local user to gain elevated privileges. Vendor package revisions must be checked because Ubuntu fixes are backported without necessarily changing the upstream version family.

fix.label: Install a fixed Ubuntu kernel
fix.text: Apply the Ubuntu security update for CVE-2023-0386, reboot into the fixed kernel, and remove unsupported old kernels after confirming successful operation.

linux-s-s-s-2-3-4-5-0-9-1-0-5-3ce6a6fb.title: Legacy Linux kernel detected
linux-s-s-s-2-3-4-5-0-9-1-0-5-3ce6a6fb.why: The running kernel belongs to an old major or minor family frequently outside normal security support. Unsupported kernels accumulate publicly documented local privilege-escalation and isolation flaws, although the exact risk depends on vendor backports and lifecycle status.

fix.label: Upgrade to a supported kernel
fix.text: Move to a vendor-supported OS and kernel stream, install all security updates, reboot into the updated kernel, and verify the old kernel is no longer running.

nopasswd-4f47cfff.title: Passwordless sudo rule
nopasswd-4f47cfff.why: A sudoers NOPASSWD rule allows the affected user to execute one or more commands without reauthentication. Broad commands, interpreters, editors, package managers, or writable command paths can make this equivalent to immediate privilege escalation.

fix.label: Require authentication and narrow scope
fix.text: Remove NOPASSWD unless noninteractive execution is essential, then allowlist only fixed root-owned commands with constrained arguments and use a dedicated service identity.

os-s-microsoft-windows-7-server-2008-ser.title: Unsupported Windows release
os-s-microsoft-windows-7-server-2008-ser.why: The host runs Windows 7, Windows Server 2008, or Windows Server 2012, releases that are outside standard support. Unless covered by an applicable extended security program, newly discovered vulnerabilities may remain unpatched and modern security controls may be unavailable.

fix.label: Migrate to a supported release
fix.text: Upgrade or replace the host with a supported Windows version, apply current cumulative updates, and isolate the system with compensating controls until migration is complete.

polkit-s-s-s-s-0-120-s-s-pwnkit-vulnerab.title: Potential PwnKit vulnerability
polkit-s-s-s-s-0-120-s-s-pwnkit-vulnerab.why: The installed polkit version is a candidate for CVE-2021-4034, a pkexec memory-corruption flaw that permits local privilege escalation to root. Because distributions backported fixes, the complete package revision and vendor advisory determine whether the host is actually vulnerable.

fix.label: Install vendor-fixed polkit
fix.text: Apply the distribution security update for CVE-2021-4034. If immediate patching is impossible, follow vendor guidance for temporarily removing the set-user-ID bit from pkexec.

privileged-s-true-bdcd4765.title: Container runs in privileged mode
privileged-s-true-bdcd4765.why: Privileged mode grants a container nearly all Linux capabilities and broad access to host devices while weakening normal isolation controls. Compromise of the container can therefore provide a direct route to host control.

fix.label: Remove privileged mode
fix.text: Recreate the workload without privileged mode, drop all capabilities by default, add only required capabilities, and expose only explicitly needed devices and host paths.

rw-r-rw-s-etc-passwd-shadow-sudoers-sudo.title: Writable account security file
rw-r-rw-s-etc-passwd-shadow-sudoers-sudo.why: An untrusted account can write /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, or a sudoers include file. Modification can create privileged users, replace password hashes, or grant unrestricted sudo access, resulting in direct root compromise.

fix.label: Restore secure ownership and mode
fix.text: Restore root ownership and vendor-recommended permissions, remove unauthorized ACLs, validate sudoers with visudo -c where applicable, and review the file for unauthorized changes.

rws-b-s-bash-sh-dash-ksh-zsh-csh-tcsh-le.title: Dangerous program has setuid root
rws-b-s-bash-sh-dash-ksh-zsh-csh-tcsh-le.why: A shell, interpreter, editor, transfer utility, debugger, or other general-purpose program has the set-user-ID bit. Many such programs can execute commands, load files, or preserve privileges, so a root-owned instance may provide a straightforward path to root.

fix.label: Restore trusted package state
fix.text: If the bit was not intentionally deployed, reinstall or verify the owning package and investigate how the permission changed.

rws-de23ca2d.title: Setuid executable present
rws-de23ca2d.why: A set-user-ID executable runs with its file owner's effective identity, commonly root. The bit may be legitimate, but vulnerable, obsolete, unexpected, or user-modifiable setuid programs can provide local privilege escalation.

fix.label: Review legitimate exceptions
fix.text: Keep only vendor-supported, root-owned setuid programs that are operationally required; patch them and ensure neither the executable nor its path is writable by untrusted users.

s-a-za-z-program-files-s-startmode-b57c0.title: Privileged Windows service candidate
s-a-za-z-program-files-s-startmode-b57c0.why: A Windows service executable under Program Files was identified together with its start mode. This is a privilege-escalation candidate when the service runs as a privileged account and its executable, directory, configuration, or unquoted path is modifiable by a lower-privileged user.

fix.label: Harden the service
fix.text: Quote paths containing spaces, remove untrusted write permissions from the executable and parent directories, use a low-privilege service account, and disable the service if unnecessary.

s-s-docker-lxd-lxc-disk-shadow-adm-b-1d9.title: Membership in a sensitive local group
s-s-docker-lxd-lxc-disk-shadow-adm-b-1d9.why: The account belongs to a group such as docker, lxd, lxc, disk, shadow, or adm. These groups can expose container-management authority, raw storage, password hashes, or sensitive logs and may provide root-equivalent access or valuable credential material.

test.label: Read sensitive group membership
test.cmd: getent group docker lxd lxc disk shadow adm

fix.label: Separate administrative duties
fix.text: Grant sensitive group membership only to dedicated administrative identities and monitor changes to those groups.

seimpersonate-dcom-reachable-roguepotato.title: Impersonation privilege with DCOM reachability
seimpersonate-dcom-reachable-roguepotato.why: The process holds SeImpersonatePrivilege and can reach the local DCOM endpoint mapper, a combination associated with named-pipe and COM token-impersonation escalation paths. No exploit is required to establish the risk: compromise of this service context may enable elevation to SYSTEM on affected configurations.

fix.label: Remove or isolate impersonation rights
fix.text: Run the service under a minimally privileged identity without SeImpersonatePrivilege where possible, apply current Windows updates, and restrict unnecessary DCOM/RPC exposure.

seimpersonate-spooler-running-printspoof.title: Impersonation privilege with active Spooler
seimpersonate-spooler-running-printspoof.why: The process has SeImpersonatePrivilege while the Print Spooler is running. This combination expands local token-impersonation attack surface and can allow a compromised service account to reach SYSTEM on susceptible configurations.

fix.label: Reduce service privilege
fix.text: Remove SeImpersonatePrivilege from service identities that do not require it and apply current Windows security updates.

serviceaccount-token-b-7f1ea010.title: Service-account token file exposed
serviceaccount-token-b-7f1ea010.why: A service-account token path is present, commonly indicating a workload credential mounted into the filesystem. Any process able to read the token may authenticate as that service account and exercise its assigned API permissions.

fix.label: Restrict and rotate the token
fix.text: Remove unnecessary token mounts, restrict file access to the workload identity, use short-lived projected tokens, minimize service-account RBAC permissions, and rotate any token that may have been exposed.

sudo-version-1-8-0-9-1-8-1-0-9-1-8-2-0-9.title: Potentially vulnerable sudo version
sudo-version-1-8-0-9-1-8-1-0-9-1-8-2-0-9.why: The detected sudo version falls in a range containing multiple historical local privilege-escalation flaws. Version matching is only a candidate signal because distributions frequently backport security fixes; the complete package revision must be compared with the vendor advisory.

fix.label: Upgrade sudo
fix.text: Install the latest vendor-supported sudo package, review the vendor changelog for backported fixes, and retest the effective sudoers policy after upgrading.

system-network-service-administrators-2a.title: Service runs under privileged identity
system-network-service-administrators-2a.why: A discovered service or process runs as SYSTEM, NETWORK SERVICE, or an administrator-class principal. If its executable, configuration, plugins, or control permissions are weak, a lower-privileged user may influence code that executes in this powerful context.

fix.label: Apply service least privilege
fix.text: Use a dedicated virtual account or gMSA with only required rights, harden service-control permissions, and remove untrusted write access from executables, configuration, and plugin directories.

unattend-ed-xml-sysprep-xml-inf-unattend.title: Unattended-install file exposed
unattend-ed-xml-sysprep-xml-inf-unattend.why: An unattended Windows setup or Sysprep file was found on disk. These files can contain administrator credentials, product keys, domain-join details, and deployment configuration that remain readable after installation.

fix.label: Remove secrets and stale files
fix.text: Delete unattended-install artifacts when no longer required, remove plaintext credentials from deployment templates, restrict remaining files to administrators, and rotate every credential found.

unshare-ru-succeeded-s-s-unprivileged-us.title: Unprivileged user namespaces enabled
unshare-ru-succeeded-s-s-unprivileged-us.why: An ordinary user can create a new user namespace and map itself to namespace root. This is intentional on some systems, but it exposes additional kernel namespace and filesystem code to unprivileged users and has been a prerequisite for numerous local privilege-escalation flaws.

fix.label: Restrict namespace creation
fix.text: If applications do not require unprivileged user namespaces, disable them using the distribution-supported sysctl or set user.max_user_namespaces to 0; otherwise keep the kernel fully patched and confine namespace-using applications.

writable-a-za-z-30aabd46.title: Writable Windows path
writable-a-za-z-30aabd46.why: A local path is writable by the assessed principal. If a privileged service, scheduled task, installer, or administrator later loads content from that location, an attacker may substitute executable or configuration data and inherit the consumer's privileges.

fix.label: Remove untrusted write access
fix.text: Restrict Modify, Write, Create Files, and Create Folders rights to the owning service or administrators, and review privileged consumers of the path before changing inherited ACLs.

writable-binary-921ba2b9.title: Writable privileged executable
writable-binary-921ba2b9.why: A service or other privileged executable can be modified by a lower-privileged principal. Replacing or patching that binary can cause attacker-controlled code to run when the service or task next starts.

test.label: Read file owner and access rules

fix.label: Harden executable permissions
fix.text: Remove write and modify rights for non-administrative principals, restore ownership to TrustedInstaller or Administrators as appropriate, and replace the binary from a trusted signed source if integrity is uncertain.

writable-pipe-1c761405.title: Writable named pipe
writable-pipe-1c761405.why: A named pipe permits access from a lower-privileged principal. If a privileged service trusts clients, fails to authenticate peers, or performs impersonation incorrectly, an attacker may inject requests, capture sensitive data, or influence privileged behavior.

fix.label: Harden pipe authorization
fix.text: Configure the server to create the pipe with an explicit restrictive security descriptor, authenticate each client, validate impersonation levels, and reject anonymous or unnecessary low-privilege access.

writable-root-runs-scripts-from-here-on-.title: Writable APT privileged script location
writable-root-runs-scripts-from-here-on-.why: A writable location supplies scripts or hooks that root executes during APT operations. An untrusted local user can alter that content and obtain root code execution when an administrator or automated updater next invokes APT.

fix.label: Review APT hook integrity
fix.text: Remove unnecessary hook directives, compare remaining scripts with trusted package or configuration-management sources, and investigate any unauthorized modifications.

b-deprecated-read-only-kubelet-b-ec66886.title: Kubelet read-only port exposed
b-deprecated-read-only-kubelet-b-ec66886.why: The deprecated kubelet read-only port can disclose pod specifications, node metadata, environment details, and workload topology without authentication. Attackers can use this information to identify secrets, privileged workloads, and paths for lateral movement.

test.label: List pods through the read-only endpoint

fix.label: Disable the read-only port
fix.text: Set the kubelet option --read-only-port=0 and expose only the authenticated HTTPS endpoint with authorization enabled.

fix.label: Restrict kubelet access
fix.text: Permit the secure kubelet port only from authorized control-plane and monitoring networks.

b-jenkins-gitlab-sonarqube-grafana-prome.title: Development or monitoring service exposed
b-jenkins-gitlab-sonarqube-grafana-prome.why: An externally reachable Jenkins, GitLab, SonarQube, Grafana, or Prometheus instance expands the administrative attack surface and may disclose software versions or operational metadata. Weak authentication, unsafe defaults, or unpatched components can turn simple discovery into credential theft or infrastructure compromise.

fix.label: Limit management-plane exposure
fix.text: Place the service behind a VPN, identity-aware proxy, or management network and allow access only from approved sources.

fix.label: Harden the application
fix.text: Enable strong authentication and MFA where supported, remove anonymous access, and keep the application and plugins patched.

balg-none-b-4f564b03.title: JWT accepts or advertises alg=none
balg-none-b-4f564b03.why: A JSON Web Token using the none algorithm has no cryptographic signature. If the application accepts such tokens where signed tokens are required, an attacker can forge identity or authorization claims.

test.label: Replay the supplied token against a read-only endpoint

fix.label: Enforce an algorithm allowlist
fix.text: Configure the JWT library to accept only the explicitly intended signing algorithm and reject none regardless of the token header.

fix.label: Validate every security claim
fix.text: Verify the signature, issuer, audience, expiration, and not-before claims before trusting token content.

banon-auth-b-465b30a5.title: Anonymous service authentication enabled
banon-auth-b-465b30a5.why: The service permits access without an accountable user identity, potentially exposing files, metadata, or administrative functionality. Attackers can inventory or retrieve accessible content without obtaining credentials, while defenders lose reliable attribution.

fix.label: Disable anonymous authentication
fix.text: Require named accounts backed by a managed identity store and grant each account only the minimum required read or write permissions.

fix.label: Restrict network access
fix.text: Expose the service only to approved clients and management networks.

bcassandra-unauth-cql-ac0e71d3.title: Cassandra CQL accepts unauthenticated access
bcassandra-unauth-cql-ac0e71d3.why: An unauthenticated Cassandra native transport endpoint may allow remote users to enumerate keyspaces and read application data. Depending on role permissions and configuration, the same access could also permit destructive database operations.

fix.label: Enable Cassandra authentication
fix.text: Configure PasswordAuthenticator or an approved external authenticator, enable authorization, and replace permissive default roles.

fix.label: Restrict native transport
fix.text: Allow the CQL port only from application and administration networks and enable client-to-node TLS.

bconsul-unauth-agent-api-7a30187a.title: Consul agent API allows anonymous access
bconsul-unauth-agent-api-7a30187a.why: The Consul agent API can disclose node identity, services, checks, datacenter details, and network topology. Some agent endpoints can change local state, so anonymous reachability also indicates a potentially broader control-plane exposure.

test.label: Read agent metadata without a token

fix.label: Enable Consul ACL enforcement
fix.text: Enable ACLs with default_policy set to deny, remove anonymous-token privileges, and issue narrowly scoped tokens to workloads.

fix.label: Bind and filter the API
fix.text: Bind HTTP interfaces to trusted addresses and restrict access with host firewalls or security groups.

bconsul-unauth-kv-dump-high-value-715888.title: Consul key-value data exposed anonymously
bconsul-unauth-kv-dump-high-value-715888.why: Anonymous callers can retrieve Consul KV entries, which commonly contain service configuration, endpoints, tokens, or credentials. A recursive dump can provide an attacker with high-value secrets and a detailed map of internal systems.

fix.label: Deny anonymous KV access
fix.text: Enable Consul ACLs with a deny-by-default policy and grant prefix-specific read access only to required workloads.

fix.label: Rotate exposed secrets
fix.text: Treat credentials found in anonymously readable KV records as compromised, rotate them, and move secrets to an appropriate secrets manager.

bcritical-jenkins-groovy-script-console-.title: Jenkins Groovy script console reachable
bcritical-jenkins-groovy-script-console-.why: The Jenkins script console executes Groovy inside the controller process and is effectively operating-system-level administrative access. If an unauthorized or compromised administrator can reach it, the controller, stored credentials, agents, and build environment may all be compromised.

fix.label: Restrict administrative access
fix.text: Limit Overall/Administer permission to a small administrator group protected by MFA and restrict controller access to a management network.

fix.label: Monitor console use
fix.text: Enable audit logging and alert on script-console requests; investigate any use that is not tied to an approved administrative change.

bcritical-unauth-clickhouse-b-72d2b408.title: ClickHouse accepts unauthenticated queries
bcritical-unauth-clickhouse-b-72d2b408.why: An unauthenticated ClickHouse endpoint may expose databases, schemas, and analytical data to any reachable client. Permissions available to the anonymous or default user may also enable costly queries or changes, increasing confidentiality and availability risk.

test.label: Query the server version without credentials

fix.label: Require authenticated users
fix.text: Disable passwordless remote use of the default account and create named users with strong authentication and least-privilege profiles.

fix.label: Restrict and encrypt access
fix.text: Limit ClickHouse interfaces to trusted networks and enable TLS for client connections.

bcritical-unauth-nats-b-fcf83e67.title: NATS broker permits unauthenticated clients
bcritical-unauth-nats-b-fcf83e67.why: A NATS broker without authentication may allow any reachable client to inspect account information and interact with subjects. Unauthorized subscriptions can disclose messages, while unauthorized publishing can affect applications and control flows.

fix.label: Enable NATS authentication
fix.text: Require NKeys, JWT-based accounts, credentials, or mutual TLS and apply subject-level publish and subscribe permissions.

fix.label: Restrict broker reachability
fix.text: Expose client, cluster, and monitoring ports only to explicitly authorized networks.

bcve-2022-0543-candidate-b-ec7e6cec.title: Redis CVE-2022-0543 candidate
bcve-2022-0543-candidate-b-ec7e6cec.why: The detected Redis instance appears potentially affected by the Debian-specific Lua sandbox escape CVE-2022-0543. A reachable EVAL capability on a vulnerable package can let an authenticated Redis user escape the Lua sandbox, but version and package provenance must be confirmed before declaring vulnerability.

test.label: Read Redis build and version details

fix.label: Install the vendor-fixed package
fix.text: Upgrade Redis using the supported Debian or Ubuntu security repository to a package version listed as fixed by the distribution.

fix.label: Reduce Redis exposure
fix.text: Require authentication, bind Redis to trusted interfaces, enforce network filtering, and remove EVAL permissions from users that do not need scripting.

beval-scripting-reachable-b-69a50af1.title: Redis EVAL scripting is remotely available
beval-scripting-reachable-b-69a50af1.why: Redis Lua scripting is available to the tested client, increasing the impact of compromised credentials or an exposed Redis service. Scripting is legitimate functionality, but vulnerable versions and overly broad command permissions can turn it into a code-execution or availability risk.

fix.label: Remove unnecessary scripting rights
fix.text: Use Redis ACLs to deny EVAL and EVALSHA to application identities that do not explicitly require server-side Lua.

fix.label: Patch and isolate Redis
fix.text: Run a supported Redis release and permit connections only from trusted application and administration networks.

bhadoop-jmx-endpoint-exposed-dd698ded.title: Hadoop JMX endpoint exposed
bhadoop-jmx-endpoint-exposed-dd698ded.why: Hadoop JMX endpoints reveal detailed runtime, host, filesystem, queue, and cluster metrics. This information helps attackers map the environment and may expose sensitive configuration values or operational identifiers.

fix.label: Restrict the HTTP management interface
fix.text: Permit Hadoop web and JMX endpoints only from authenticated monitoring systems and management networks.

fix.label: Enable secure Hadoop operation
fix.text: Use Kerberos-secured Hadoop, TLS, service authorization, and an authenticated proxy where web access is required.

bhadoop-namenode-ui-exposed-a60d53ee.title: Hadoop NameNode UI exposed
bhadoop-namenode-ui-exposed-a60d53ee.why: The NameNode web interface can disclose filesystem paths, node inventory, storage capacity, cluster health, and software versions. Public reachability gives attackers valuable reconnaissance and may expose additional unauthenticated administrative endpoints.

fix.label: Move the UI to a management boundary
fix.text: Restrict NameNode web interfaces to administrators and monitoring systems through firewall rules or an authenticated reverse proxy.

fix.label: Enable Hadoop web authentication
fix.text: Configure Kerberos/SPNEGO authentication and TLS for Hadoop web consoles.

bhmac-brute-the-secret-b-23317e71.title: JWT uses a brute-forceable HMAC signature
bhmac-brute-the-secret-b-23317e71.why: HMAC-signed tokens rely on one shared secret for both signing and verification. If that secret is weak, an attacker who obtains a token can test guesses offline and then forge arbitrary identity or authorization claims.

fix.label: Replace weak signing secrets
fix.text: Generate a high-entropy secret with an approved cryptographic random generator, store it in a secrets manager, and rotate all tokens after replacement.

fix.label: Consider asymmetric signatures
fix.text: Use an approved asymmetric JWT algorithm when multiple services verify tokens so verifiers do not need access to the signing key.

binfluxdb-unauth-query-api-fc5f9a20.title: InfluxDB query API allows anonymous access
binfluxdb-unauth-query-api-fc5f9a20.why: An unauthenticated InfluxDB query endpoint can disclose database names, measurements, infrastructure telemetry, and application metrics. Operational data often reveals internal hosts, credentials embedded in tags, and behavior useful for further attacks.

fix.label: Require authenticated API access
fix.text: Enable authentication and issue narrowly scoped tokens or users for each writer, reader, and monitoring integration.

fix.label: Restrict the query port
fix.text: Allow InfluxDB API access only from approved application and administration networks and use TLS.

binsecure-apiserver-b-d69cfcc5.title: Kubernetes insecure API server exposed
binsecure-apiserver-b-d69cfcc5.why: An insecure Kubernetes API endpoint accepts requests without normal authentication and authorization protections. Reachability can expose cluster objects and, depending on enabled methods, may permit full cluster takeover.

fix.label: Disable insecure serving
fix.text: Remove obsolete insecure-port and insecure-bind-address settings and serve the API only over authenticated TLS.

fix.label: Enforce authorization and network controls
fix.text: Use RBAC or another supported authorization mode and restrict API server reachability to approved clients.

bjenkins-user-enumeration-exposed-77ad88.title: Jenkins user enumeration exposed
bjenkins-user-enumeration-exposed-77ad88.why: The Jenkins interface reveals valid account identifiers to unauthenticated or low-privilege users. Confirmed usernames improve password-spraying and phishing accuracy and may expose personal or organizational naming conventions.

fix.label: Require authentication for user data
fix.text: Disable anonymous read access and ensure account and people endpoints require an authorized Jenkins identity.

fix.label: Strengthen account defenses
fix.text: Use centralized authentication, MFA where supported, rate limiting, and monitoring for failed-login patterns.

bkafka-unauth-broker-94c84874.title: Kafka broker permits unauthenticated access
bkafka-unauth-broker-94c84874.why: An unauthenticated Kafka broker exposes cluster metadata and topic names to any reachable client. If authorization is also absent or permissive, attackers may consume sensitive messages or publish data that disrupts downstream applications.

fix.label: Enable broker authentication
fix.text: Configure SASL or mutual TLS for every listener and remove plaintext unauthenticated listeners.

fix.label: Enforce Kafka ACLs
fix.text: Enable an authorizer, deny access by default, and grant topic and consumer-group rights only to required principals.

bkibana-api-responds-b-416b14a3.title: Kibana API reachable
bkibana-api-responds-b-416b14a3.why: A reachable Kibana API exposes a management surface associated with Elasticsearch data and saved objects. Even when authentication is present, external exposure and version disclosure increase the opportunity for credential attacks and exploitation of unpatched components.

fix.label: Restrict Kibana exposure
fix.text: Place Kibana behind an authenticated proxy or VPN and permit access only from approved user and management networks.

fix.label: Enable Elastic security controls
fix.text: Require authentication, apply least-privilege Kibana roles, use TLS, and keep Kibana aligned with a supported Elasticsearch release.

blua-rce-cve-2024-31449-candidate-b-81da.title: Redis CVE-2024-31449 candidate
blua-rce-cve-2024-31449-candidate-b-81da.why: The Redis version and available Lua functionality indicate possible exposure to CVE-2024-31449, a stack overflow in Lua bit-library commands that may lead to code execution. The finding is a candidate until the exact Redis version is compared with vendor-fixed releases; no exploit attempt is necessary.

fix.label: Upgrade to a fixed Redis release
fix.text: Upgrade to Redis 6.2.16, 7.2.6, 7.4.1, or a later supported release containing the vendor fix.

fix.label: Constrain scripting access
fix.text: Use Redis ACLs to deny EVAL and EVALSHA to identities that do not require Lua and restrict Redis to trusted networks.

bmqtt-unauth-broker-b-2c618f3f.title: MQTT broker permits anonymous clients
bmqtt-unauth-broker-b-2c618f3f.why: An MQTT broker accepting anonymous clients may expose telemetry and operational topics to unauthorized subscribers. If publish permissions are also open, attackers could inject commands or falsified sensor data into connected systems.

test.label: Read the broker version topic anonymously

fix.label: Disable anonymous clients
fix.text: Set anonymous access off and require password, certificate, or external identity authentication.

fix.label: Apply topic ACLs
fix.text: Grant each client only the publish and subscribe topics it requires and use TLS for client connections.

bneo4j-default-cred-neo4j-neo4j-worked-f.title: Neo4j default credentials accepted
bneo4j-default-cred-neo4j-neo4j-worked-f.why: The built-in neo4j/neo4j credentials are still valid, allowing anyone who knows the product defaults to authenticate. Database contents, relationships, and potentially administrative procedures are exposed according to that account's privileges.

test.label: Run a harmless query with default credentials

fix.label: Replace the default password
fix.text: Set a unique, high-entropy administrator password immediately and invalidate any sessions or credentials derived from the default account.

fix.label: Apply least privilege
fix.text: Use separate named accounts and roles for applications and administrators, and restrict Bolt and HTTP access to trusted networks.

bneo4j-unauth-http-api-58500a90.title: Neo4j HTTP API exposed without authentication
bneo4j-unauth-http-api-58500a90.why: The Neo4j HTTP interface responds without requiring an authenticated identity. Depending on version and endpoint permissions, attackers may enumerate database metadata or submit read queries against graph data.

test.label: Check the legacy database API anonymously
Inspect the Neo4j HTTP service root

fix.label: Require Neo4j authentication
fix.text: Enable authentication, remove anonymous access, and assign least-privilege roles to application identities.

fix.label: Restrict HTTP and Bolt listeners
fix.text: Bind database interfaces to trusted addresses, filter them at the network boundary, and enable TLS.

boracle-tns-sids-discovered-85744d13.title: Oracle TNS service identifiers exposed
boracle-tns-sids-discovered-85744d13.why: The Oracle listener disclosed valid service names or SIDs, confirming a reachable database service and reducing the uncertainty required for later authentication attempts. Service identifiers, versions, and listener details help attackers target specific databases and known vulnerabilities.

test.label: Confirm a supplied service with authorized credentials
test.cmd:
printf 'set heading off feedback off
select instance_name from v$instance;
exit
' | sqlplus -s '<user>/<pass>@//<host>:<port>/<service>'

fix.label: Restrict Oracle listener access
fix.text: Permit the listener port only from authorized application and administration hosts and disable unnecessary listener services.

fix.label: Reduce listener disclosure
fix.text: Apply current Oracle security updates, configure secure listener registration, and avoid exposing detailed service information to untrusted networks.

bredis-sentinel-b-master-topology-672336.title: Redis Sentinel topology exposed
bredis-sentinel-b-master-topology-672336.why: Redis Sentinel reveals monitored master names, addresses, replica topology, and failover state. This disclosure maps high-value Redis nodes and may enable unauthorized Sentinel control operations if authentication and ACLs are also weak.

fix.label: Authenticate Sentinel clients
fix.text: Configure supported Redis ACL or password authentication for Sentinel and require authentication between Sentinel and Redis nodes.

fix.label: Isolate Sentinel ports
fix.text: Allow Sentinel traffic only among approved Redis, Sentinel, and administrative hosts.

brsync-high-value-module-exposed-daedaa1.title: High-value rsync module exposed
brsync-high-value-module-exposed-daedaa1.why: A reachable rsync module can expose directory names and files without requiring a filesystem login. High-value modules may contain backups, source code, configuration, keys, or other sensitive data suitable for credential theft and lateral movement.

test.label: List a supplied module without downloading

fix.label: Limit module access
fix.text: Use hosts allow and hosts deny controls, require authentication, and expose only directories explicitly needed by approved clients.

fix.label: Remove sensitive content
fix.text: Do not export secrets, private keys, unrestricted backups, or writable deployment paths through rsync modules.

bsolr-cores-exposed-ceb00229.title: Solr core inventory exposed
bsolr-cores-exposed-ceb00229.why: The Solr administration API exposes core names, instance directories, document counts, and status information. Core names and deployment details assist reconnaissance and may reveal additional query or administrative endpoints.

fix.label: Enable Solr authentication and authorization
fix.text: Protect administrative and collection APIs with supported authentication plugins and least-privilege authorization rules.

fix.label: Restrict the Solr administration surface
fix.text: Permit Solr access only from required applications and management networks; do not publish the admin UI directly.

bspark-ui-applications-api-exposed-cb7d2.title: Spark applications API exposed
bspark-ui-applications-api-exposed-cb7d2.why: The Spark monitoring API can disclose application names, users, job stages, executor hosts, logs, and performance details. This operational metadata maps internal compute resources and may contain sensitive arguments or paths.

fix.label: Require authenticated UI access
fix.text: Place Spark UIs and history servers behind an authenticated proxy and configure appropriate access-control filters.

fix.label: Restrict monitoring ports
fix.text: Allow UI and REST API access only from approved user, monitoring, and management networks.

bsplunk-mgmt-api-unauth-aab28122.title: Splunk management API allows anonymous access
bsplunk-mgmt-api-unauth-aab28122.why: The Splunk management API can disclose server configuration, indexes, applications, users, and deployment details. Anonymous access may expose security telemetry itself and, if broader endpoints are open, create a path to administrative compromise.

fix.label: Require management API authentication
fix.text: Remove anonymous capabilities, enforce strong named-account authentication, and apply least-privilege Splunk roles.

fix.label: Isolate the management port
fix.text: Restrict port 8089 or the configured management port to administrators and trusted Splunk components.

bstorage-iscsi-target-exposed-48ec7863.title: iSCSI target exposed
bstorage-iscsi-target-exposed-48ec7863.why: An exposed iSCSI target reveals storage target names and portal topology to remote initiators. If access controls or CHAP are weak, unauthorized systems may connect to block devices, risking data disclosure, corruption, and filesystem damage.

test.label: Perform target discovery without logging in

fix.label: Restrict initiators and networks
fix.text: Use target ACLs and network filtering so only approved initiator IQNs and storage-network addresses can reach the target.

fix.label: Authenticate storage sessions
fix.text: Enable mutual CHAP or IPsec where supported and keep iSCSI traffic on a dedicated, non-routed storage network.

bstorage-minio-ceph-radosgw-object-gatew.title: Storage management service reachable
bstorage-minio-ceph-radosgw-object-gatew.why: A reachable MinIO, Ceph/RADOSGW, Ceph monitor, or Gluster management interface exposes a high-value storage control or data plane. Version and topology disclosure aid reconnaissance, while weak authentication could expose buckets, objects, cluster state, or administrative operations.

fix.label: Segment storage interfaces
fix.text: Limit data and management ports to explicitly authorized application, storage, and administration networks.

fix.label: Enforce service authentication
fix.text: Use unique service identities, least-privilege policies, TLS, and supported authentication mechanisms; remove default or anonymous access.

bunauth-couchbase-mgmt-b-b4140a91.title: Couchbase management API exposed anonymously
bunauth-couchbase-mgmt-b-b4140a91.why: Anonymous Couchbase management access can disclose cluster nodes, buckets, services, memory allocation, and software versions. If privileged management endpoints share the same exposure, attackers may gain control over database configuration and data availability.

fix.label: Require Couchbase authentication
fix.text: Enable role-based access control, remove anonymous management access, and use separate least-privilege accounts for applications and administrators.

fix.label: Restrict management ports
fix.text: Expose Couchbase administration interfaces only to a dedicated management network and enable TLS.

bunauth-docker-etcd-v2-keys-kubelet-apis.title: Container control-plane API exposed anonymously
bunauth-docker-etcd-v2-keys-kubelet-apis.why: An unauthenticated Docker, etcd, kubelet, or Kubernetes API exposes sensitive workload and cluster state to any reachable client. These interfaces can contain secrets and frequently include state-changing operations, so anonymous access may lead to host or cluster compromise.

fix.label: Require authenticated TLS
fix.text: Disable plaintext or anonymous listeners and require client authentication plus authorization for every control-plane API.

fix.label: Isolate control-plane ports
fix.text: Permit API access only among approved cluster components and administrative systems.

fix.label: Rotate exposed secrets
fix.text: Review anonymously accessible API output and rotate any service-account tokens, credentials, or certificates it exposed.

bunauth-gitlab-api-exposed-ca3c738d.title: GitLab API exposes data anonymously
bunauth-gitlab-api-exposed-ca3c738d.why: The GitLab API returns project, user, version, or instance information without authentication. Even when some public access is intentional, the exposed metadata can reveal repositories, namespaces, account names, and software versions useful for targeted attacks.

test.label: Check the exposed API version endpoint

fix.label: Review anonymous visibility
fix.text: Disable public visibility where it is not a business requirement and require authentication for internal projects, users, and instance metadata.

fix.label: Restrict and patch GitLab
fix.text: Limit administrative interfaces to trusted networks, enforce MFA for privileged users, and maintain a supported GitLab release.

bunauth-grafana-datasources-exposed-a6f1.title: Grafana data sources exposed anonymously
bunauth-grafana-datasources-exposed-a6f1.why: The Grafana API exposes configured data-source names, types, URLs, and identifiers without authentication. This maps internal monitoring and database systems and may reveal stored secrets on vulnerable or misconfigured versions.

fix.label: Disable anonymous API access
fix.text: Disable anonymous authentication unless explicitly required and ensure data-source administration requires a privileged role.

fix.label: Rotate potentially exposed credentials
fix.text: Patch Grafana, inspect the response for sensitive values, and rotate any data-source credentials that may have been disclosed.

bunauth-jenkins-api-exposed-ebd449e2.title: Jenkins API exposed anonymously
bunauth-jenkins-api-exposed-ebd449e2.why: Anonymous Jenkins API access can disclose jobs, builds, nodes, plugins, parameters, and repository details. This information aids credential attacks and supply-chain targeting, while overly permissive anonymous permissions may expose build artifacts or trigger capabilities.

fix.label: Remove anonymous permissions
fix.text: Use a supported authorization strategy and grant anonymous users no access unless a narrowly documented public use case exists.

fix.label: Protect Jenkins access
fix.text: Place Jenkins on a management network, require strong centralized authentication, and keep the controller and plugins patched.

bunauth-jira-serverinfo-exposed-a75ffe0d.title: Jira server information exposed
bunauth-jira-serverinfo-exposed-a75ffe0d.why: The Jira REST API discloses product version, deployment type, build number, and base URL without authentication. Exact version data lets attackers quickly select relevant advisories and tailor social-engineering or exploitation attempts.

fix.label: Limit anonymous REST access
fix.text: Require authentication for server metadata where supported and restrict Jira to intended user networks or an authenticated access proxy.

fix.label: Maintain a supported Jira release
fix.text: Apply Atlassian security updates promptly and avoid exposing detailed version headers through proxies or error pages.

bunauth-prometheus-config-exposed-9ee7e8.title: Prometheus configuration exposed
bunauth-prometheus-config-exposed-9ee7e8.why: The Prometheus status API exposes scrape targets, job definitions, file paths, remote endpoints, and configuration structure without authentication. The data maps internal services and may reveal embedded credentials or bearer-token locations.

fix.label: Protect Prometheus with an access layer
fix.text: Restrict the listener to trusted networks or place it behind a reverse proxy providing authentication and TLS.

fix.label: Remove secrets from exposed configuration
fix.text: Use protected secret files or a secrets manager, minimize configuration visibility, and rotate any credentials disclosed by the endpoint.

bunauth-redis-b-1a97399e.title: Redis accepts unauthenticated clients
bunauth-redis-b-1a97399e.why: A Redis server that accepts unauthenticated commands may expose cached data, sessions, queues, keys, and server configuration. Depending on command permissions and deployment hardening, attackers could also alter data or abuse dangerous administrative features.

fix.label: Enable Redis ACL authentication
fix.text: Disable or tightly constrain the default user and create named ACL users with strong credentials and command/key restrictions.

fix.label: Restrict and encrypt Redis traffic
fix.text: Bind Redis to trusted interfaces, enforce firewall rules, enable protected mode, and use TLS where traffic crosses host boundaries.

bunauth-rethinkdb-b-5b87cecc.title: RethinkDB exposed without authentication
bunauth-rethinkdb-b-5b87cecc.why: An unauthenticated RethinkDB service may reveal databases, tables, cluster nodes, and administrative state. If query or web-administration access is unrestricted, attackers may read or change application data and cluster configuration.

fix.label: Require RethinkDB authentication
fix.text: Set a strong admin password, create least-privilege application users, and remove passwordless accounts.

fix.label: Bind interfaces securely
fix.text: Do not bind the driver, cluster, or web administration ports to untrusted interfaces; enforce firewall filtering and TLS.

bunauth-sonarqube-system-info-exposed-10.title: SonarQube system information exposed
bunauth-sonarqube-system-info-exposed-10.why: The SonarQube API discloses system status, edition, version, plugins, or runtime details without authentication. This information supports vulnerability matching and reveals the structure of an important source-code analysis system.

fix.label: Require authenticated API access
fix.text: Disable force-authentication exceptions that are not required and limit system-information permissions to administrators.

fix.label: Restrict and patch SonarQube
fix.text: Expose SonarQube only to intended development networks and keep it on a supported, fully patched release.

bunauth-tomcat-host-manager-exposed-8a74.title: Tomcat Host Manager exposed anonymously
bunauth-tomcat-host-manager-exposed-8a74.why: The Tomcat Host Manager controls virtual hosts and is intended only for trusted administrators. Anonymous access indicates a severe authorization failure that may expose host configuration and administrative operations.

test.label: Request the Host Manager interface anonymously

fix.label: Remove or restrict Host Manager
fix.text: Undeploy the host-manager application when unused; otherwise require a dedicated strong account with only the necessary host-manager role.

fix.label: Limit management-network access
fix.text: Apply Tomcat RemoteCIDRValve or equivalent network controls so only approved administration hosts can reach the interface.

bunauth-tomcat-manager-exposed-004a31c6.title: Tomcat Manager exposed anonymously
bunauth-tomcat-manager-exposed-004a31c6.why: Tomcat Manager provides application inventory, deployment, session, and lifecycle functions. Anonymous access can disclose deployed applications and may expose deployment operations capable of compromising the entire Tomcat host.

test.label: Read the text application list if exposed

fix.label: Remove or secure Manager
fix.text: Undeploy the manager application when unnecessary; otherwise require a strong dedicated account and grant only the specific manager role needed.

fix.label: Restrict management access
fix.text: Allow Manager access only from approved administration addresses using Tomcat valves and network firewalls.

bzookeeper-4lw-exposed-103b92c9.title: ZooKeeper four-letter commands exposed
bzookeeper-4lw-exposed-103b92c9.why: ZooKeeper four-letter-word commands disclose health, client connections, watches, environment details, and cluster state without using the normal data authorization model. The information can map dependent systems, and some commands may impose unnecessary server load.

fix.label: Allowlist required commands
fix.text: Set 4lw.commands.whitelist to the smallest required set, typically only health checks, and disable commands that expose detailed state.

fix.label: Restrict client-port access
fix.text: Limit ZooKeeper connectivity to ensemble members and authorized application or monitoring hosts.

bzookeeper-config-exposed-high-value-7ed.title: ZooKeeper configuration exposed
bzookeeper-config-exposed-high-value-7ed.why: The ZooKeeper conf command reveals server paths, ports, timing settings, quorum configuration, and other high-value deployment details. Attackers can use this information to map the ensemble and identify adjacent management or data services.

fix.label: Disable the conf command
fix.text: Remove conf from 4lw.commands.whitelist and retain only commands explicitly required for health monitoring.

fix.label: Isolate ZooKeeper
fix.text: Restrict client and quorum ports to trusted systems and enable supported client authentication and TLS.

solr-reachable-1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8-0-9-8-10-.title: Legacy Apache Solr version reachable
solr-reachable-1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8-0-9-8-10-.why: The reachable Solr instance reports a legacy release in the detected version range, including versions that are end-of-life or missing later security fixes. Exposure of an obsolete search service increases the likelihood that known authentication, information-disclosure, or code-execution vulnerabilities are applicable.

fix.label: Upgrade to a supported Solr release
fix.text: Plan and test an upgrade to a currently supported Solr major and patch release, including compatible Java, configuration, and client changes.

fix.label: Protect Solr during migration
fix.text: Enable authentication and authorization, restrict network access, and review Apache Solr security advisories for the exact installed version.

baggressive-mode-psk-hash-harvested-0f76.title: IKEv1 aggressive-mode PSK hash exposed
baggressive-mode-psk-hash-harvested-0f76.why: The VPN completed IKEv1 aggressive-mode negotiation and disclosed material that permits offline guessing of the group pre-shared key. Recovering a weak PSK can enable unauthorized VPN negotiation and compromise every peer sharing that secret.

fix.label: Disable aggressive mode
fix.text: Disable IKEv1 aggressive mode and migrate peers to IKEv2 with certificate-based authentication.

fix.label: Rotate the exposed PSK
fix.text: Replace the shared secret with a long random value after disabling the weak exchange, and use unique credentials for separate peer groups.

bajp-responding-without-auth-b-ecbc49c7.title: Unauthenticated AJP connector exposed
bajp-responding-without-auth-b-ecbc49c7.why: The AJP connector accepts requests without a connector secret and is reachable outside its trusted reverse-proxy tier. AJP permits greater manipulation of application-server request attributes than HTTP, and vulnerable or permissive configurations can expose application files or backend functionality.

fix.label: Restrict and authenticate AJP
