fix.text: Bind the connector to a private or loopback address, restrict it to authorized proxy addresses, and configure a strong AJP secret with secretRequired enabled.

fix.label: Remove unnecessary AJP
fix.text: Disable the AJP connector when the deployment does not require it, and keep Tomcat or the applicable servlet container fully patched.

bauth-bypass-b-749346eb.title: Authentication bypass detected
bauth-bypass-b-749346eb.why: The collected evidence indicates that a protected service or operation can be reached without satisfying its intended authentication check. Because this rule is product-neutral, defenders should identify the affected component and validate the precise bypass condition before determining its full impact.

test.label: Confirm the exposed product and version

fix.label: Apply the product-specific correction
fix.text: Identify the exact product, version, and bypass path from the evidence; apply the vendor patch or configuration correction and invalidate any sessions or credentials that may have been exposed.

fix.label: Add a trusted enforcement layer
fix.text: Restrict the service to approved networks and ensure authorization is enforced server-side for every protected operation, not only in a client or reverse-proxy interface.

bcipher-0-b-bcd10171.title: IPMI cipher suite 0 enabled
bcipher-0-b-bcd10171.why: The BMC accepts IPMI 2.0 cipher suite 0, which provides no authentication or integrity protection and can permit access using a valid username without its password. BMC access can bypass operating-system controls and expose console, virtual-media, firmware, and power-management functions.

fix.label: Disable cipher suite 0
fix.text: Disable cipher suite 0 for every IPMI privilege level using the BMC vendor's management interface, then verify it remains disabled after firmware upgrades or resets.

fix.label: Isolate BMC interfaces
fix.text: Place BMCs on a dedicated management network, filter UDP 623 to authorized administration systems, update firmware, and rotate BMC credentials.

bcors-b-breflect-04062725.title: CORS origin reflection
bcors-b-breflect-04062725.why: The application reflects an arbitrary Origin value in its CORS response, indicating an overly broad trust policy. If credentialed cross-origin requests are also allowed and sensitive responses are readable, an attacker-controlled site can access data using a victim's authenticated browser session.

fix.label: Use an exact origin allowlist
fix.text: Return Access-Control-Allow-Origin only for explicitly approved origins; parse and compare the complete scheme, host, and port instead of reflecting request input or matching loose suffixes.

fix.label: Limit credentialed CORS
fix.text: Disable Access-Control-Allow-Credentials unless it is required, and exclude sensitive endpoints and response headers from cross-origin access.

bcritical-radius-access-accept-to-bogus-.title: RADIUS accepts invalid credentials
bcritical-radius-access-accept-to-bogus-.why: The RADIUS server returned Access-Accept for a deliberately invalid identity, indicating a fail-open policy, incorrect identity-store mapping, or unsafe catch-all rule. Any network access device relying on this policy may admit unauthorized users to VPN, wireless, or administrative networks.

fix.label: Correct the authorization policy
fix.text: Default to Access-Reject when the identity is unknown, the credential check fails, or an upstream identity source is unavailable; remove catch-all acceptance rules.

fix.label: Test policy regressions
fix.text: Add automated negative tests using nonexistent users and invalid passwords for each RADIUS virtual server, realm, and network-access policy.

bcups-unauth-518ab9d3.title: Unauthenticated CUPS service exposed
bcups-unauth-518ab9d3.why: A remote client can access the CUPS service without authentication and enumerate server or printer information. Depending on operation policies, the exposure can reveal queues and jobs or permit unauthorized printing and administrative actions.

fix.label: Restrict remote access
fix.text: Bind CUPS only to required interfaces and use cupsd location rules or a firewall to permit trusted print clients and administrators only.

fix.label: Require protected operations
fix.text: Require authentication for printer management and sensitive IPP operations, disable remote administration when unnecessary, and use TLS for authenticated connections.

bcups-unauth-and-potentially-vuln-b-40d3.title: CUPS exposure with vulnerable-version signal
bcups-unauth-and-potentially-vuln-b-40d3.why: The unauthenticated CUPS endpoint reported a version associated with the 2024 cups-browsed vulnerability chain. A version banner alone does not prove exploitability because distribution backports and UDP 631 reachability matter, but an affected cups-browsed deployment can accept untrusted printer advertisements that lead to malicious printer configuration and code execution when used.

fix.label: Update the affected packages
fix.text: Install vendor-fixed cups-browsed, cups-filters, libcupsfilters, and libppd packages; use the distribution advisory rather than upstream version strings to account for backports.

fix.label: Disable legacy browsing
fix.text: Stop and disable cups-browsed if automatic remote-printer discovery is not required, and block inbound UDP 631 from untrusted networks.

bcve-d-4-d-4-7-b-b-candidate-vulnerable-.title: CVE candidate or vulnerable-version signal
bcve-d-4-d-4-7-b-b-candidate-vulnerable-.why: A scanner associated the observed product or version with a published CVE, but the generic signal does not by itself establish that the vulnerable code path is present or unpatched. Defenders should account for product edition, configuration, platform, and vendor backports before declaring the vulnerability confirmed.

test.label: Review the CVE and version evidence

fix.label: Validate against the vendor advisory
fix.text: Map the detected build and configuration to the exact affected and fixed versions in the vendor advisory, including operating-system package backports.

fix.label: Patch or mitigate
fix.text: Apply the vendor update or documented workaround, restrict the affected service while remediation is pending, and repeat the non-destructive version check afterward.

bfinger-responds-with-user-info-b-03a484.title: Finger service discloses user information
bfinger-responds-with-user-info-b-03a484.why: The Finger service returns account, login, or activity information to unauthenticated remote clients. Attackers can use the disclosed usernames and host activity to improve password attacks, social engineering, and targeting.

fix.label: Disable the legacy service
fix.text: Disable fingerd or its inetd/systemd socket activation unless there is a documented business requirement.

fix.label: Restrict required access
fix.text: If Finger must remain available, filter TCP 79 to specific management systems and configure the daemon to minimize user details.

bflexnet-flexlm-license-server-reachable.title: FlexNet license server reachable
bflexnet-flexlm-license-server-reachable.why: A FlexNet/FLEXlm license manager is reachable from the tested network. Even without confirmed data disclosure, the service identifies valuable engineering software infrastructure and exposes an administrative protocol that is normally intended for controlled internal clients.

fix.label: Limit license-service reachability
fix.text: Use host firewalls and network ACLs to allow only approved license clients and administration systems to reach lmgrd and every vendor-daemon port.

fix.label: Pin vendor-daemon ports
fix.text: Configure fixed vendor-daemon ports so firewall rules cover the entire license path, and update lmgrd, vendor daemons, and administration utilities.

bflexnet-unauth-lmstat-disclosure-fb2ca9.title: Unauthenticated FlexNet lmstat disclosure
bflexnet-unauth-lmstat-disclosure-fb2ca9.why: The license server answers lmstat queries without authenticating the requester, exposing licensed products, feature names, users, and client hostnames. This information maps high-value engineering systems and supplies valid identity and workstation data for subsequent attacks.

fix.label: Enforce network isolation
fix.text: FlexNet deployments commonly rely on network controls rather than request authentication; restrict lmgrd and vendor-daemon ports to approved client subnets and administration hosts.

fix.label: Reduce exposed user data
fix.text: Use supported secure utilities or no-user-information options where available, review INCLUDE and EXCLUDE policies, and avoid exposing the service across user or perimeter networks.

bimap-plaintext-auth-allowed-auth-succes.title: IMAP permits plaintext password authentication
bimap-plaintext-auth-allowed-auth-succes.why: The IMAP service advertises or accepted a password-based authentication exchange that is not adequately protected by transport encryption. Network observers can capture reusable mailbox credentials, which are often also valid for webmail, directory, or single-sign-on services.

test.label: Validate credentials only through required TLS

fix.label: Require encrypted transport
fix.text: Disable cleartext authentication before TLS, require STARTTLS or implicit TLS, and reject authentication when encryption negotiation fails.

fix.label: Retire legacy authentication
fix.text: Prefer modern token or challenge-based authentication where supported, disable unused IMAP service exposure, and rotate credentials that may have crossed plaintext links.

bjetdirect-pjl-unauth-a6716c58.title: Unauthenticated JetDirect/PJL interface
bjetdirect-pjl-unauth-a6716c58.why: The raw printing port accepts PJL commands without authenticating the client. PJL can disclose device identity, configuration, status, and sometimes filesystem or stored-job information; writable operations may also alter printer behavior.

fix.label: Restrict raw printing
fix.text: Allow TCP 9100 only from authorized print servers and client networks, and disable JetDirect/raw printing when IPP through a controlled print server is sufficient.

fix.label: Harden the printer
fix.text: Update printer firmware, disable unused PJL filesystem and job-retention features, set administrative credentials, and clear unneeded stored jobs.

blpd-reachable-45a47068.title: Legacy LPD printing service reachable
blpd-reachable-45a47068.why: The legacy Line Printer Daemon protocol is reachable from the tested network. LPD generally lacks modern authentication and encryption, so unnecessary exposure can permit queue enumeration, unauthorized job submission, or interception of print metadata depending on server policy.

fix.label: Replace or restrict LPD
fix.text: Disable LPD where possible and use authenticated IPP over TLS; otherwise restrict TCP 515 to designated print servers and approved clients.

fix.label: Constrain printer queues
fix.text: Remove unused queues, prevent anonymous remote administration, and configure queue-level host and user allowlists.

bnagios-nrpe-reachable-397121a9.title: Nagios NRPE service reachable
bnagios-nrpe-reachable-397121a9.why: The Nagios Remote Plugin Executor is reachable from the tested network, exposing a privileged monitoring agent and its implementation details. Reachability alone is not command execution, but weak allowed-host rules, unsafe command definitions, or obsolete NRPE versions can turn this into sensitive-data disclosure or remote command risk.

fix.label: Restrict monitoring clients
fix.text: Set allowed_hosts to only the authorized Nagios servers and enforce the same restriction with host and network firewalls.

fix.label: Harden NRPE commands
fix.text: Update NRPE, require TLS, disable arbitrary command arguments unless essential, and define narrowly scoped plugins that do not invoke a shell with untrusted input.

bnats-auth-required-false-b-43f5d2e1.title: NATS server does not require authentication
bnats-auth-required-false-b-43f5d2e1.why: The NATS INFO banner states that authentication is not required, allowing anonymous clients to establish sessions. Unless subject permissions or network isolation provide an equivalent boundary, an attacker may observe messaging topology and publish or subscribe to application data.

fix.label: Require client authentication
fix.text: Configure NATS users, tokens, NKeys, or operator/account JWT credentials so unauthenticated connections are rejected.

fix.label: Apply subject authorization
fix.text: Give each application a separate identity with explicit publish and subscribe allowlists, require TLS, and restrict the client and monitoring ports at the network boundary.

bntp-amplification-vector-cve-2013-5211-.title: NTP monlist amplification exposed
bntp-amplification-vector-cve-2013-5211-.why: The NTP service responded to the legacy mode-7 monlist request associated with CVE-2013-5211. Because a small spoofed UDP request can trigger a much larger response, an attacker can abuse the host as a reflection and amplification source in distributed denial-of-service attacks.

test.label: Read basic NTP variables without monlist

fix.label: Disable monitoring queries
fix.text: Upgrade the NTP implementation and disable the legacy monitor/monlist facility; for ntpd, use the vendor-supported equivalent of disable monitor.

fix.label: Prevent reflection
fix.text: Permit UDP 123 only where required, block untrusted control queries, and implement source-address validation at network edges.

bntp-responds-to-mode-6-readvar-b-80229e.title: NTP mode-6 variables remotely readable
bntp-responds-to-mode-6-readvar-b-80229e.why: The NTP daemon answers unauthenticated mode-6 readvar control queries. These responses can disclose software versions, system details, reference sources, and peer state that help an attacker fingerprint infrastructure and identify additional weaknesses.

fix.label: Restrict NTP control queries
fix.text: Configure the daemon to deny mode-6 control access from untrusted networks while retaining only the time-synchronization traffic required by approved clients.

fix.label: Reduce network exposure
fix.text: Filter UDP 123 to approved peers or clients and update the NTP implementation to a supported release.

bopen-proxy-f8b23707.title: Unauthenticated open proxy
bopen-proxy-f8b23707.why: The service forwards traffic for unauthenticated remote clients. Attackers can conceal their source, reach destinations through the organization's trusted address space, consume bandwidth, and cause abusive traffic to be attributed to the proxy owner.

test.label: Send one harmless HEAD request through the proxy

fix.label: Require authorization
fix.text: Require authenticated clients and restrict permitted source networks, destination ports, protocols, and address ranges with explicit allowlists.

fix.label: Block unintended proxying
fix.text: Disable the proxy service if it is not required, deny requests to internal and link-local destinations, and restrict the listener with a firewall.

bopen-relay-candidate-b-a3a3ed2b.title: Potential SMTP open relay
bopen-relay-candidate-b-a3a3ed2b.why: The SMTP server accepted an external-to-external recipient during a relay test, indicating that unauthenticated clients may be able to relay mail. A confirmed open relay is readily abused for spam and phishing and can cause domain and IP reputation blocklisting.

test.label: Test relay acceptance without sending a message

fix.label: Restrict relay policy
fix.text: Permit relaying only for authenticated users or explicitly trusted source networks and accepted local domains; reject all other RCPT TO requests.

fix.label: Retest every listener
fix.text: Check IPv4, IPv6, submission, and perimeter SMTP listeners after changing policy, and monitor logs for previous unauthorized relay activity.

bpop3-plaintext-auth-allowed-auth-succes.title: POP3 permits plaintext password authentication
bpop3-plaintext-auth-allowed-auth-succes.why: The POP3 service advertises or accepted reusable password authentication without adequate transport encryption. Anyone able to observe the connection can capture mailbox credentials, which may also provide access to other organizational systems.

test.label: Validate credentials only through required TLS

fix.label: Require encrypted transport
fix.text: Disable authentication on unencrypted POP3 sessions and require STARTTLS or implicit TLS with valid certificates.

fix.label: Reduce legacy mail exposure
fix.text: Disable POP3 when it is not required, prefer modern authentication where supported, and rotate credentials that may have traversed plaintext connections.

bradius-blastradius-cve-2024-3596-precon.title: BlastRADIUS message-authenticator gap
bradius-blastradius-cve-2024-3596-precon.why: The RADIUS service responded to an Access-Request that did not carry a valid Message-Authenticator, satisfying a key precondition for CVE-2024-3596. On networks where an attacker can intercept and modify RADIUS traffic, this protocol weakness can permit alteration of an Access-Reject into an Access-Accept.

fix.label: Install BlastRADIUS updates
fix.text: Upgrade every RADIUS server, proxy, and network-access client to vendor-fixed versions; mixed unpatched paths can preserve the vulnerable condition.

fix.label: Require packet authentication
fix.text: Require Message-Authenticator on Access-Request packets and enable the vendor's Proxy-State validation control, such as FreeRADIUS require_message_authenticator and limit_proxy_state.

brealvnc-b-bbypass-b-f7c5fe0d.title: RealVNC authentication bypass
brealvnc-b-bbypass-b-f7c5fe0d.why: The VNC server appears vulnerable to CVE-2006-2369, in which affected RealVNC releases accept a client-selected security type that bypasses the configured password check. Successful bypass grants interactive access to the remote desktop with the privileges of the logged-in session.

fix.label: Upgrade RealVNC
fix.text: Replace RealVNC 4.1.0 or 4.1.1 with a supported fixed release and verify that the server no longer accepts the None security type.

fix.label: Restrict remote desktop access
fix.text: Permit VNC only through a managed VPN or administration network, require strong authentication, and block direct exposure at host and perimeter firewalls.

bremote-command-execution-b-ca19f4c9.title: Remote command-execution condition detected
bremote-command-execution-b-ca19f4c9.why: The evidence contains a remote-command-execution finding, indicating that network input may cross a trust boundary and execute with service or host privileges. Because this rule is product-neutral, defenders must identify the exact component, affected version, and prerequisites without executing a proof-of-concept payload.

fix.label: Patch and contain the component
fix.text: Apply the vendor fix or remove the affected feature, restrict the service to trusted management paths, and treat the host as potentially compromised if it was exposed to untrusted clients.

fix.label: Investigate for exploitation
fix.text: Review service, process, authentication, and network logs for exploitation indicators; rotate reachable secrets and rebuild from trusted media when integrity cannot be established.

bsip-service-cfa45a0d.title: SIP signaling service exposed
bsip-service-cfa45a0d.why: A SIP endpoint is reachable from the tested network and reveals a voice-signaling attack surface. Exposure alone is not proof of compromise, but permissive registration, weak credentials, verbose responses, or unsafe dial plans can enable extension discovery, toll fraud, call interception, and service disruption.

fix.label: Restrict SIP sources
fix.text: Allow SIP signaling only from approved trunks, session border controllers, phones, and management networks; block direct Internet access when it is not explicitly required.

fix.label: Harden voice authentication
fix.text: Require strong per-device credentials, disable anonymous registration and unused methods, constrain dial plans, enable TLS/SRTP where supported, and monitor anomalous call attempts.

bslp-amplification-vector-cve-2023-29552.title: SLP reflection/amplification exposure
bslp-amplification-vector-cve-2023-29552.why: The SLP service produced a disproportionately large discovery response, indicating exposure to the reflection/amplification behavior documented as CVE-2023-29552. An attacker capable of spoofing UDP source addresses can direct amplified traffic at third-party victims and consume the organization's network resources.

test.label: Perform one direct SLP information query

fix.label: Disable unnecessary SLP
fix.text: Disable SLP on systems that do not require service discovery, especially Internet-facing or management appliances.

fix.label: Filter and patch
fix.text: Block UDP and TCP 427 at perimeter boundaries, restrict internal access to required clients, and apply vendor updates or SLP-disablement guidance.

bslp-service-type-list-exposed-high-valu.title: SLP service catalog exposed
bslp-service-type-list-exposed-high-valu.why: The SLP registry disclosed numerous service types without authentication. This catalog can reveal internal printers, storage systems, virtualization infrastructure, management services, and other high-value targets that may not otherwise be discoverable.

fix.label: Reduce SLP visibility
fix.text: Disable SLP where it is unnecessary or bind it only to dedicated management interfaces and required service-discovery networks.

fix.label: Enforce network boundaries
fix.text: Filter TCP and UDP 427 between security zones and ensure registered services do not advertise sensitive management endpoints beyond their intended clients.

bssdp-upnp-responder-b-256bafda.title: SSDP/UPnP responder exposed
bssdp-upnp-responder-b-256bafda.why: The host responds to SSDP discovery and may disclose device type, management URLs, model information, and UPnP services. Exposure across trust boundaries aids reconnaissance and, when reachable from the Internet, may also contribute to UDP reflection abuse.

fix.label: Disable unnecessary UPnP
fix.text: Disable UPnP/SSDP on routers, endpoints, and appliances that do not require automatic local discovery.

fix.label: Confine discovery traffic
fix.text: Block UDP 1900 across perimeter and routed trust boundaries, and limit SSDP multicast and unicast responses to the intended local segment.

btelnet-open-device-129976a8.title: Telnet management service exposed
btelnet-open-device-129976a8.why: A Telnet service is reachable on the device, exposing an obsolete remote terminal protocol with no transport encryption or server authentication. Credentials and administrative commands can be observed or altered by anyone positioned on the network path.

fix.label: Replace Telnet with SSH
fix.text: Disable the Telnet daemon or device management option and use SSH with modern algorithms, strong credentials, and preferably public-key authentication.

fix.label: Restrict management access
fix.text: Place device management interfaces on a dedicated network and permit access only from approved administration hosts.

bterrapin-ssh-audit-66181601.title: SSH Terrapin attack exposure
bterrapin-ssh-audit-66181601.why: The SSH service supports a vulnerable protocol and algorithm combination associated with CVE-2023-48795, commonly called Terrapin. An active network attacker may truncate portions of the SSH handshake and weaken negotiated security features; the scanner signal should be interpreted alongside the server and client patch levels.

test.label: Audit SSH algorithms and strict key exchange

fix.label: Install SSH fixes
fix.text: Update SSH servers and clients to vendor-fixed releases that implement strict key exchange, such as OpenSSH 9.6 or a vendor-backported equivalent.

fix.label: Disable vulnerable combinations
fix.text: Until all peers are patched, disable ChaCha20-Poly1305 and CBC with Encrypt-then-MAC combinations identified as vulnerable by the vendor, while retaining approved modern alternatives.

btftp-readable-config-f856f6cb.title: Configuration file readable over TFTP
btftp-readable-config-f856f6cb.why: The TFTP server permits unauthenticated retrieval of a configuration file. Network-device and provisioning configurations frequently contain topology details, password hashes, SNMP communities, VPN secrets, or other credentials that enable broader compromise.

test.label: Retrieve the known file to standard output

fix.label: Remove sensitive files
fix.text: Remove configurations, backups, keys, and credentials from the TFTP root; rotate every secret contained in a file that was anonymously readable.

fix.label: Constrain or replace TFTP
fix.text: Restrict TFTP to a dedicated provisioning network and approved clients, enforce a minimal read-only root, or replace it with an authenticated encrypted transfer mechanism.

bunauth-git-daemon-b-39d5d84c.title: Unauthenticated Git repository export
bunauth-git-daemon-b-39d5d84c.why: The Git daemon exposes at least one repository without authenticating readers. Repository history may disclose proprietary source, deleted files, internal infrastructure details, and credentials that remain recoverable from earlier commits.

fix.label: Stop anonymous export
fix.text: Remove git-daemon-export-ok from private repositories, do not use git daemon --export-all, and disable the daemon if anonymous read access is unnecessary.

fix.label: Use authenticated repository access
fix.text: Serve private repositories through authenticated SSH or HTTPS, restrict network access, scan the full history for secrets, and rotate any exposed credentials.

bvpn-cisco-anyconnect-asa-ssl-vpn-fortin.title: Internet-facing SSL VPN identified
bvpn-cisco-anyconnect-asa-ssl-vpn-fortin.why: The endpoint was fingerprinted as a supported enterprise SSL VPN product, placing a high-value remote-access control plane in scope. Product detection is not itself proof of a vulnerability, but VPN gateways are frequent targets for credential attacks and pre-authentication flaws and should receive expedited version and configuration review.

fix.label: Maintain the edge appliance
fix.text: Verify the exact product and build, apply current vendor security updates, remove unsupported versions, and review relevant CISA KEV entries and vendor advisories.

fix.label: Harden remote access
fix.text: Require phishing-resistant MFA, disable unused portals and management interfaces, restrict administration to a separate trusted network, and monitor authentication and configuration changes.

bvrfy-enabled-b-03eb095d.title: SMTP VRFY command enabled
bvrfy-enabled-b-03eb095d.why: The SMTP server processes VRFY requests and may distinguish valid local recipients from nonexistent users. Attackers can use this behavior to build accurate account lists for phishing, password attacks, and business-email-compromise targeting.

fix.label: Disable useful VRFY responses
fix.text: Configure the MTA to reject VRFY or return an identical non-enumerable response for valid and invalid users; for Postfix, enable disable_vrfy_command.

fix.label: Limit account-enumeration signals
fix.text: Apply consistent recipient handling, rate limits, and monitoring across VRFY, EXPN, RCPT TO, webmail, and directory interfaces.

bx11-open-display-b-ee0898b0.title: Unauthenticated X11 display access
bx11-open-display-b-ee0898b0.why: The X11 display accepts remote client connections without effective authorization. An attacker may be able to observe windows, capture input, inject keyboard or mouse events, or interact with applications running in the victim's graphical session.

fix.label: Disable direct TCP X11
fix.text: Start the X server with TCP listening disabled and remove display-manager settings that expose ports 6000 and above.

fix.label: Restore access controls
fix.text: Remove permissive xhost entries, use per-session Xauthority cookies, and provide necessary remote GUI access through tightly controlled SSH forwarding.

byarn-resourcemanager-unauth-dda5ab1e.title: Unauthenticated YARN ResourceManager API
byarn-resourcemanager-unauth-dda5ab1e.why: The Hadoop YARN ResourceManager REST API returns cluster information without authenticating the requester. It can disclose cluster topology and configuration, and deployments that also leave administrative APIs unprotected may permit application submission or control with worker-level execution impact.

fix.label: Enable Hadoop authentication
fix.text: Enable Kerberos-based Hadoop security and SPNEGO for ResourceManager HTTP endpoints, then enforce YARN service-level authorization and queue ACLs.

fix.label: Restrict the management plane
fix.text: Expose ResourceManager interfaces only to authorized users, gateway services, and administration networks; block direct access from untrusted segments.

byarn-unauth-app-inventory-d7eaf3ca.title: YARN application inventory exposed
byarn-unauth-app-inventory-d7eaf3ca.why: Unauthenticated clients can enumerate YARN applications, including names, users, queues, states, and tracking URLs. This reveals active workloads and privileged identities and may expose linked application interfaces or sensitive operational metadata.

test.label: List a bounded set of applications

fix.label: Authenticate ResourceManager HTTP access
fix.text: Enable Kerberos/SPNEGO authentication and Hadoop authorization for the ResourceManager web and REST interfaces.

fix.label: Limit inventory visibility
fix.text: Restrict ResourceManager and tracking URLs to approved networks and users, and review proxy-user and queue ACLs for least privilege.

bzabbix-agent-unauth-metric-query-9c344b.title: Unauthenticated Zabbix agent queries
bzabbix-agent-unauth-metric-query-9c344b.why: The Zabbix agent returns metric values to an unauthenticated remote requester. Exposed item keys can reveal operating-system, network, process, filesystem, and application details, and unsafe user parameters or system.run rules can raise the impact substantially.

fix.label: Restrict permitted servers
fix.text: Set the agent Server parameter to only authorized Zabbix servers or proxies and enforce the same source restriction with a host firewall.

fix.label: Require encryption and constrain keys
fix.text: Configure TLS with PSK or certificates, allow only required item keys, explicitly deny system.run and sensitive file-reading keys, and remove unsafe user parameters.

bzabbix-server-reachable-bfba7fc4.title: Zabbix server port reachable
bzabbix-server-reachable-bfba7fc4.why: The Zabbix server listener is reachable from the tested network, exposing a high-value monitoring control-plane component. Reachability alone does not demonstrate unauthenticated access, but unnecessary exposure increases opportunities for version fingerprinting, protocol attacks, and attempts to impersonate trusted agents or proxies.

fix.label: Restrict component communication
fix.text: Allow the server port only from registered Zabbix proxies, active agents, and required internal components using network and host firewalls.

fix.label: Protect and maintain the server
fix.text: Require certificate- or PSK-protected component connections, keep Zabbix supported and patched, and separate the web interface, database, and server listener by role.

cve-2024-6387-regresshion-27d5471e.title: OpenSSH regreSSHion candidate
cve-2024-6387-regresshion-27d5471e.why: The SSH banner matches an OpenSSH release range associated with CVE-2024-6387, a pre-authentication race condition in sshd's signal handling that can lead to remote code execution on affected glibc-based systems. Banner matching is only a candidate signal because operating-system vendors may backport fixes without changing the upstream version string, and some platforms are not exploitable.

test.label: Record the SSH implementation and algorithms

fix.label: Install the vendor-fixed OpenSSH package
fix.text: Upgrade to OpenSSH 9.8 or the operating-system vendor's patched package, and verify patch status through the package changelog or advisory rather than the banner alone.

fix.label: Apply temporary containment
fix.text: Until patched, restrict SSH to trusted administration sources; setting LoginGraceTime to 0 prevents the vulnerable timeout path but can increase denial-of-service exposure and should be treated only as a temporary vendor-documented mitigation.

b-rubrik-cohesity-backup-dell-powerprote.title: Enterprise backup management API exposed
b-rubrik-cohesity-backup-dell-powerprote.why: A reachable Rubrik, Cohesity, or Dell PowerProtect API identifies a high-value management plane that commonly holds infrastructure inventories and privileged integration credentials. Attackers target backup systems to steal data and impair recovery before disruptive operations.

fix.label: Restrict management access
fix.text: Place the backup API on a dedicated management network and permit access only from approved administration hosts and monitoring systems.

fix.label: Harden administrator authentication
fix.text: Require MFA or centralized identity for administrators, remove dormant accounts, rotate integration credentials, and install supported security updates.

bartifact-docker-registry-sonatype-nexus.title: Artifact repository or registry exposed
bartifact-docker-registry-sonatype-nexus.why: An exposed Docker Registry, Nexus, Artifactory, or Harbor service reveals a software-supply-chain management plane and may disclose repository names, versions, or internal package metadata. Compromise of a privileged account could let an attacker obtain proprietary artifacts or tamper with software consumed by deployment pipelines.

fix.label: Limit registry reachability
fix.text: Expose the service only to authorized developer, CI, and administration networks through firewall rules or an authenticated reverse proxy.

fix.label: Enforce repository controls
fix.text: Disable anonymous access unless explicitly required, apply least-privilege repository roles, require MFA for administrators, and use separate scoped CI tokens.

bartifact-docker-registry-unauth-catalog.title: Docker Registry catalog allows anonymous access
bartifact-docker-registry-unauth-catalog.why: The registry catalog can be listed without authentication, exposing repository names and potentially enabling anonymous tag or manifest enumeration. These details reveal internal applications and versions that help attackers identify sensitive images and vulnerable components.

fix.label: Require registry authentication
fix.text: Configure the registry or its reverse proxy to require authentication for catalog, repository, tag, manifest, pull, and push operations.

fix.label: Restrict network access
fix.text: Limit registry access to approved CI workers, deployment systems, and administrator networks.

bauth-ok-b-18ccdbe4.title: RabbitMQ management credentials accepted
bauth-ok-b-18ccdbe4.why: Operator-supplied credentials successfully authenticated to the RabbitMQ management API. Depending on their assigned tags and virtual-host permissions, the account may expose users, queues, exchanges, messages, connections, or administrative functions.

fix.label: Review the authenticated account
fix.text: Confirm that the account is expected, rotate it if its use is unexplained, and restrict its RabbitMQ tags and virtual-host permissions to the minimum required.

fix.label: Protect the management API
fix.text: Restrict management API access to administration networks, require TLS, and use centralized authentication or MFA where supported.

bbmc-hpe-ilo-dell-idrac-supermicro-ipmi-.title: Server baseboard management controller exposed
bbmc-hpe-ilo-dell-idrac-supermicro-ipmi-.why: A reachable iLO, iDRAC, IPMI, XCC, IMM, or CIMC interface provides out-of-band control that can remain available even when the operating system is offline. Administrative compromise may permit console access, power control, virtual-media mounting, firmware changes, or recovery bypass.

fix.label: Isolate out-of-band management
fix.text: Move BMC interfaces to a dedicated management network with firewall or jump-host enforcement and no direct Internet or user-LAN access.

fix.label: Harden controller access
fix.text: Change default credentials, disable unused legacy protocols, require MFA where supported, install current firmware, and forward audit events to monitoring.

bcommvault-detected-5f2f4842.title: Commvault management service exposed
bcommvault-detected-5f2f4842.why: A reachable Commvault web service exposes a backup-management plane with visibility into protected systems, stored data, and operational credentials. Attackers frequently target backup infrastructure to obtain broad access and prevent reliable restoration.

fix.label: Restrict CommServe access
fix.text: Allow the web service only from dedicated administration and backup networks, preferably through a controlled jump host.

fix.label: Harden and update Commvault
fix.text: Apply supported maintenance releases, require strong administrator authentication, rotate service credentials, and review roles and audit logs.

bdefault-cred-6077e4eb.title: Default credentials accepted
bdefault-cred-6077e4eb.why: A service accepted a vendor-default or commonly shipped credential pair. Attackers routinely test these credentials because they can provide immediate administrative access without exploiting a software vulnerability.

fix.label: Replace the default credential
fix.text: Set a unique, randomly generated password or managed service credential and invalidate every vendor-default account or secret.

fix.label: Check for prior use
fix.text: Review authentication and configuration logs for access using the default credential, rotate related secrets, and investigate unexplained activity.

bdell-avamar-powerprotect-legacy-service.title: Legacy Avamar or PowerProtect service reachable
bdell-avamar-powerprotect-legacy-service.why: A legacy Dell Avamar or PowerProtect service is reachable over the network, increasing the attack surface of a system that stores or controls backups. Older management protocols may lack modern authentication and transport protections and should not be accessible from general-purpose networks.

test.label: Confirm and fingerprint the TCP service

fix.label: Restrict the legacy service
fix.text: Allow the port only between documented backup components on a dedicated network and block it from user, guest, and Internet-facing segments.

fix.label: Upgrade or retire the interface
fix.text: Install current supported PowerProtect or Avamar releases and disable legacy listeners that are no longer required.

bhypervisor-vmware-esxi-host-proxmox-ve-.title: Hypervisor management plane exposed
bhypervisor-vmware-esxi-host-proxmox-ve-.why: A VMware ESXi, Proxmox VE, or Nutanix Prism management interface is reachable. These systems control many workloads, so stolen administrator access or exploitation can expose virtual disks, consoles, snapshots, credentials, and multiple hosted services at once.

fix.label: Segment hypervisor management
fix.text: Permit access only from a dedicated management network and approved jump hosts; block direct access from user networks and the Internet.

fix.label: Harden privileged access
fix.text: Require MFA or centralized identity, remove unused local administrators, apply security updates, and alert on privileged logins and configuration changes.

bkey-only-b-adfd43e9.title: SSH permits public-key authentication only
bkey-only-b-adfd43e9.why: The SSH server advertises public-key authentication but not password or keyboard-interactive authentication. This reduces password-spraying risk, but defenders must still protect private keys, constrain authorized keys, and remove stale access because possession of a trusted key may be sufficient for login.

test.label: Read advertised SSH authentication methods
test.cmd: ssh -vv -p <port> -o BatchMode=yes -o PreferredAuthentications=none -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null <user>@<host> true 2>&1 | grep -i 'authentication methods'

fix.label: Maintain key-only authentication
fix.text: Keep password authentication disabled, inventory authorized keys, remove stale keys, and require passphrases or hardware-backed keys for privileged access.

fix.label: Constrain key privileges
fix.text: Apply least privilege to SSH accounts and use authorized_keys restrictions such as source-address, command, or forwarding constraints where appropriate.

bopenstack-keystone-detected-856681df.title: OpenStack Keystone API exposed
bopenstack-keystone-detected-856681df.why: A reachable Keystone endpoint identifies the identity control plane for an OpenStack environment and can disclose API versions and service topology. Although version discovery may be intentionally public, unnecessary reachability increases reconnaissance value and exposes a high-impact authentication surface.

fix.label: Restrict identity API exposure
fix.text: Expose administrative Keystone endpoints only to trusted management networks and publish only the interfaces required by legitimate clients.

fix.label: Harden Keystone
fix.text: Use TLS, federated or MFA-protected administrative identities, least-privilege roles, supported releases, and centralized audit logging.

bplatform-hashicorp-nomad-portainer-ranc.title: Workload platform control plane exposed
bplatform-hashicorp-nomad-portainer-ranc.why: A Nomad, Portainer, Rancher, or Argo CD control plane is reachable and reveals a high-value workload-management surface. Compromised access could expose cluster inventories, deployment configuration, registry credentials, secrets, or the ability to alter running applications.

test.label: Probe product discovery endpoints
test.cmd: for p in /v1/status/leader /api/status /v3/settings/server-version /api/version; do curl -k -i '<service>://<host>:<port>'"$p"; done

fix.label: Restrict control-plane access
fix.text: Limit the interface to trusted administration and cluster networks through firewall rules, a VPN, or an authenticated access proxy.

fix.label: Enforce strong authorization
fix.text: Enable the product's authentication and authorization features, require SSO and MFA for administrators, use scoped automation tokens, and remove anonymous access.

bplatform-nomad-unauth-job-inventory-f09.title: Nomad job inventory accessible anonymously
bplatform-nomad-unauth-job-inventory-f09.why: The Nomad jobs API returns workload inventory without authentication. Job names, namespaces, types, and deployment metadata reveal internal architecture and can guide attacks against applications, images, or supporting services.

fix.label: Enable Nomad ACLs
fix.text: Enable the Nomad ACL system, set an appropriate default-deny policy, and grant job-listing permissions only to authenticated identities that require them.

fix.label: Limit API reachability
fix.text: Bind or firewall the HTTP API so it is reachable only from trusted cluster and administration networks, and require TLS for remote clients.

bpotential-cred-leak-b-314c9b48.title: Potential credentials exposed through search data
bpotential-cred-leak-b-314c9b48.why: A read-only Elasticsearch query found documents matching credential-related terms such as passwords, secrets, or tokens. Search indexes often aggregate logs and application records, so anonymous or overprivileged query access can expose reusable credentials at scale.

fix.label: Require authenticated search access
fix.text: Enable Elasticsearch security, block anonymous cluster access, and grant index privileges only to applications and users with a documented need.

fix.label: Remove and rotate exposed secrets
fix.text: Identify the originating data source, purge unnecessary secret-bearing records according to retention policy, and rotate every credential that may have been indexed.

brmi-registry-02db4e39.title: Java RMI registry exposed
brmi-registry-02db4e39.why: A reachable Java RMI registry can disclose bound object names, remote endpoints, and implementation details. Exposed registries also increase the risk from unsafe remote-object configurations or vulnerable applications registered behind them.

fix.label: Restrict registry reachability
fix.text: Bind the registry to an internal interface where possible and firewall it so only explicitly authorized application hosts can connect.

fix.label: Harden registered services
fix.text: Remove obsolete bindings, avoid exposing unsafe remote methods or serialized-object entry points, and update the JRE and hosting application.

bslp-open-service-registry-b7a3b96f.title: Service Location Protocol registry exposed
bslp-open-service-registry-b7a3b96f.why: A reachable SLP service registry permits network clients to discover advertised services and related attributes. Internet or broad-network exposure assists reconnaissance and may also expose implementations affected by historical SLP vulnerabilities or amplification abuse.

test.label: Check for a TCP SLP listener

fix.label: Disable SLP when unnecessary
fix.text: Disable the SLP daemon or product integration if service discovery is not required.

fix.label: Constrain SLP traffic
fix.text: Permit SLP only within the smallest required management segment and block TCP and UDP port 427 at external and inter-segment boundaries.

bsource-ci-gerrit-atlassian-confluence-a.title: Source or Atlassian service exposed
bsource-ci-gerrit-atlassian-confluence-a.why: A Gerrit, Confluence, Jira, or Bamboo interface is reachable and may reveal project names, users, versions, build information, or internal documentation. These systems frequently contain source-code context and integration credentials, making their administrative and anonymous-access boundaries important attack paths.

test.label: Probe product information endpoints
test.cmd: for p in /config/server/version /status /rest/api/2/serverInfo /rest/api/latest/info; do curl -k -i '<service>://<host>:<port>'"$p"; done

fix.label: Restrict anonymous visibility
fix.text: Disable unneeded anonymous project, issue, page, build, and user-directory access and review all public or broadly shared content.

fix.label: Protect administration
fix.text: Require SSO and MFA for administrators, apply current vendor security updates, scope integration tokens, and restrict management interfaces to trusted networks.

bsource-ci-teamcity-github-enterprise-az.title: Enterprise source or CI service exposed
bsource-ci-teamcity-github-enterprise-az.why: A TeamCity, GitHub Enterprise, or Azure DevOps Server interface is reachable and may expose organization, repository, build, or version metadata. These platforms hold source code and powerful automation credentials, so compromised access can affect both intellectual property and the software supply chain.

test.label: Probe service metadata endpoints
test.cmd: for p in /app/rest/server /api/v3/meta '/_apis/connectionData?connectOptions=0'; do curl -k -i '<service>://<host>:<port>'"$p"; done

fix.label: Limit external reachability
fix.text: Publish only required user-facing endpoints and restrict administrative, agent, and maintenance interfaces to trusted networks.

fix.label: Harden identities and tokens
fix.text: Require SSO and MFA, disable anonymous access, use short-lived least-privilege automation tokens, protect build agents, and apply vendor security updates promptly.

bthickclient-rdp-creds-vpn-profile-brows.title: Local client credential artifact present
bthickclient-rdp-creds-vpn-profile-brows.why: An RDP credential reference, VPN profile, or browser login database exists on the assessed workstation. Even when values are encrypted, an attacker with local user access may recover connection targets, usernames, tokens, or secrets using the user's security context.

fix.label: Remove unnecessary saved access
fix.text: Delete obsolete profiles and cached credentials through the owning application, and configure clients to avoid retaining credentials where operationally practical.

fix.label: Protect workstation secrets
fix.text: Use full-disk encryption, strong screen-lock policy, endpoint protection, and separate privileged accounts; require MFA for RDP and VPN services.

bthickclient-sshkey-at-rest-saved-sessio.title: High-risk client secret stored locally
bthickclient-sshkey-at-rest-saved-sessio.why: A private SSH key, saved session, credential store, or configuration secret was found on the workstation. Local compromise could turn these artifacts into immediate access to servers, databases, file-transfer systems, or administrative interfaces.

fix.label: Move secrets into managed storage
fix.text: Replace plaintext or reversibly stored credentials with an approved password manager, operating-system credential vault, hardware-backed key, or short-lived identity mechanism.

fix.label: Rotate affected credentials
fix.text: Rotate any key, password, or token whose local protection or access history cannot be assured, then remove stale saved sessions and secret-bearing configuration files.

bunauth-proxmox-version-api-exposed-8638.title: Proxmox version API accessible anonymously
bunauth-proxmox-version-api-exposed-8638.why: The Proxmox API returns release, version, and repository information without authentication. This gives attackers a reliable product fingerprint for vulnerability matching and confirms the location of a high-impact virtualization management plane.

fix.label: Restrict the Proxmox API
fix.text: Limit management-interface access to a dedicated administration network, VPN, or authenticated proxy even if the version endpoint itself cannot be disabled.

fix.label: Maintain current packages
fix.text: Apply supported Proxmox VE and Debian security updates and monitor the management plane for unexpected reconnaissance and login activity.

buser-exists-b-90f92a5a.title: XMPP account existence can be inferred
buser-exists-b-90f92a5a.why: The XMPP authentication flow produced a response or repeatable timing difference that may distinguish an existing username. Reliable account enumeration helps attackers construct targeted password-spraying and social-engineering campaigns, although results should be compared with randomized controls to exclude uniform SASL failures.

test.label: Repeat SASL differential checks with controls

fix.label: Normalize authentication failures
fix.text: Configure or update the XMPP server and identity backend so nonexistent and valid accounts receive indistinguishable SASL failure responses and comparable processing times.

fix.label: Limit automated probing
fix.text: Rate-limit failed authentication attempts, monitor distributed enumeration patterns, require MFA where supported, and avoid exposing unnecessary user-directory information.

bvault-not-initialized-claim-init-opport.title: HashiCorp Vault is not initialized
bvault-not-initialized-claim-init-opport.why: The Vault API reports that the instance has not been initialized. The first party to initialize it receives the initial root token and key shares, so an attacker who reaches this state could claim control of the new Vault before its owner completes provisioning.

fix.label: Restrict access immediately
fix.text: Block untrusted network access to the Vault API before initialization; do not allow testing personnel or unattended automation to initialize the instance.

fix.label: Perform a controlled initialization ceremony
fix.text: Have designated custodians initialize Vault using the approved seal design, securely distribute recovery material, protect the initial root token, and revoke it after setup.

bveeam-b-r-rest-detected-dbcaa69e.title: Veeam Backup REST API exposed
bveeam-b-r-rest-detected-dbcaa69e.why: A reachable Veeam Backup & Replication REST endpoint identifies a high-value backup-management system and may disclose version or authentication details. Veeam servers commonly possess broad infrastructure access, and vulnerable or stolen administrative access can undermine both protected workloads and recovery data.

fix.label: Restrict the REST API
fix.text: Allow API access only from designated backup administration hosts and automation systems on a protected management network.

fix.label: Patch and protect Veeam
fix.text: Install current Veeam security updates, require strong unique administrative identities, rotate service credentials, and monitor privileged API activity.

bveritas-netbackup-detected-8aa2feba.title: Veritas NetBackup service exposed
bveritas-netbackup-detected-8aa2feba.why: A reachable NetBackup service reveals backup infrastructure that may communicate with many protected hosts and storage systems. Compromise can expose backup data, privileged service relationships, and the organization's ability to recover from destructive activity.

fix.label: Restrict NetBackup communications
fix.text: Permit the service only between documented NetBackup components and administration hosts on protected backup networks.

fix.label: Update and audit NetBackup
fix.text: Apply supported security fixes, remove obsolete clients and trust relationships, rotate service credentials, and review administrator and restore activity.

bvmware-vcenter-sdk-reachable-24c791fc.title: VMware vCenter SDK endpoint exposed
bvmware-vcenter-sdk-reachable-24c791fc.why: The vCenter SDK endpoint is reachable and exposes the automation interface for managing virtual infrastructure. While authentication is normally required, unnecessary reachability provides a precise management-plane target and increases the impact of stolen credentials or unpatched vulnerabilities.

fix.label: Restrict SDK access
fix.text: Allow the SDK only from approved management and automation hosts, and block it from Internet-facing and user workstation networks.

fix.label: Harden API identities
fix.text: Use dedicated least-privilege service accounts, rotate automation credentials, require MFA for human administrators, and keep vCenter fully patched.

bvmware-vcenter-ui-a99e5695.title: VMware vCenter management UI exposed
bvmware-vcenter-ui-a99e5695.why: A reachable vCenter web interface identifies the central management plane for VMware infrastructure. Compromised administrative access can affect numerous virtual machines, networks, datastores, snapshots, and console sessions.

fix.label: Segment vCenter management
fix.text: Restrict the UI to a dedicated management network, approved jump hosts, or a strongly authenticated administrative access proxy.

fix.label: Protect administrator access
fix.text: Require MFA through the configured identity provider, remove stale privileged accounts, apply vCenter updates, and alert on unusual login or role changes.

defaultpassword-4522eb4c.title: Windows AutoLogon password stored in registry
defaultpassword-4522eb4c.why: The Winlogon registry configuration contains a DefaultPassword value used for automatic logon. Any principal able to read the value can recover a plaintext Windows credential that may also be valid for remote access or other systems.

fix.label: Disable plaintext AutoLogon
fix.text: Disable automatic logon and remove DefaultPassword from Winlogon; use a managed kiosk or service-account design when unattended startup is required.

fix.label: Rotate the account password
fix.text: Change the affected account password and investigate whether it was reused or accessed by unauthorized local principals.

password-passwd-secret-api-key-token-s-s.title: Possible plaintext secret in a file
password-passwd-secret-api-key-token-s-s.why: A file contains a password-, secret-, API-key-, or token-like assignment with a nonempty value. The match requires validation because configuration examples can cause false positives, but a real value may grant access to applications, cloud services, databases, or infrastructure.

test.label: Confirm matching files without printing values

fix.label: Move the secret out of the file
fix.text: Store production secrets in an approved secret manager or protected operating-system credential facility and inject them only at runtime.

fix.label: Rotate confirmed secrets
fix.text: Revoke and replace any genuine credential found in plaintext, remove it from backups and version history where feasible, and restrict access to residual files.

password-passwd-secret-api-key-token-s-s.title: Possible plaintext secret on Windows
password-passwd-secret-api-key-token-s-s.why: A Windows enumeration artifact contains a password-, secret-, API-key-, or token-like assignment. Examples and placeholders can match the pattern, but a real value may expose local, domain, application, or cloud access and should be treated as compromised until validated.

test.label: Review the file access control list

fix.label: Use managed secret storage
fix.text: Move the value to Windows Credential Manager, DPAPI-protected application storage, a managed service account, or an enterprise secret manager as appropriate.

fix.label: Rotate and remove the value
fix.text: Revoke confirmed credentials, replace them with unique scoped secrets, remove plaintext copies and stale backups, and restrict the containing file's ACL.

rw-s-sid-rsa-ed25519-ecdsa-dsa-b-23e3e3c.title: SSH private key stored on disk
rw-s-sid-rsa-ed25519-ecdsa-dsa-b-23e3e3c.why: A file named like a standard SSH private key is present in the assessed user context. If the key lacks a strong passphrase or can be read by an attacker, it may provide direct access to every system that trusts its corresponding public key.

fix.label: Protect and rotate the key
fix.text: Use a strong passphrase or hardware-backed key, rotate keys whose confidentiality is uncertain, and remove the old public key from every authorized_keys file and service that trusted it.

LIN-OS-RELEASE.title: OS release and kernel
LIN-OS-RELEASE.why: Accurate operating-system and kernel inventory is essential for identifying unsupported releases and matching the host to applicable security advisories. Attackers commonly exploit known vulnerabilities on obsolete or unpatched platforms.

fix.label: Maintain supported releases
fix.text: Compare the reported distribution and kernel with vendor support and security-advisory information, then upgrade any end-of-life release through the vendor-supported process.

LIN-PKG-SECUPDATES.title: Pending security updates
LIN-PKG-SECUPDATES.semantics: FAIL: >=1 pending security update in the package cache; WARN: non-security updates pending only; PASS: none. Reads cache only (apt-get -s / dnf -C), never refreshes.
LIN-PKG-SECUPDATES.why: Pending security updates leave publicly documented vulnerabilities available for exploitation. An attacker can fingerprint package versions and use a matching local or remote exploit to gain access or elevate privileges.

test.label: Inspect the cached APT upgrade plan

fix.label: Apply Debian or Ubuntu updates
fix.cmd: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get upgrade

LIN-PKG-AUTOUPDATE.title: Automatic security updates
LIN-PKG-AUTOUPDATE.semantics: PASS: unattended-upgrades / dnf-automatic enabled; WARN: not configured.
LIN-PKG-AUTOUPDATE.why: Without automatic security updates, exploitable packages can remain vulnerable until an administrator intervenes. Attackers often weaponize disclosed vulnerabilities faster than manual patch cycles can respond.

fix.label: Enable unattended upgrades on Debian or Ubuntu
fix.cmd: sudo apt-get install unattended-upgrades && sudo systemctl enable --now apt-daily-upgrade.timer

fix.label: Enable automatic updates on DNF systems
fix.text: Install dnf-automatic, set upgrade_type = security and apply_updates = yes in /etc/dnf/automatic.conf, then enable the applicable dnf-automatic timer.

LIN-REBOOT-REQUIRED.title: Reboot pending for updates
LIN-REBOOT-REQUIRED.semantics: WARN: /var/run/reboot-required present (patched kernel/libs not loaded); PASS: absent.
LIN-REBOOT-REQUIRED.why: A pending reboot can mean that updated kernels or shared libraries are installed but vulnerable code remains loaded. An attacker may continue exploiting the active old code until the host or affected services are restarted.

test.label: Check the reboot-required marker
test.cmd: if [ -e /var/run/reboot-required ]; then echo 'reboot required'; else echo 'no reboot marker'; fi

fix.label: Schedule a controlled reboot
fix.text: Validate service redundancy and maintenance requirements, then reboot the host during an approved window and confirm that /var/run/reboot-required is absent afterward.

LIN-SYSCTL-PTRACE.title: Yama ptrace scope
LIN-SYSCTL-PTRACE.semantics: WARN: kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=0; PASS: >=1; NA: Yama absent.
LIN-SYSCTL-PTRACE.why: With kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=0, same-user processes can trace one another without a parent-child relationship. A compromised process can use this access to inspect or modify an SSH agent, browser, or privileged helper and steal credentials or tokens.

LIN-SYSCTL-KPTR.title: Kernel pointer restriction
LIN-SYSCTL-KPTR.why: Unrestricted kernel pointer disclosure gives attackers address information that can weaken kernel address-space randomization. A local attacker can use exposed addresses to make kernel exploits more reliable.

LIN-SYSCTL-DMESG.title: dmesg restriction
LIN-SYSCTL-DMESG.why: Allowing unprivileged users to read the kernel log can expose kernel addresses, device details, and security-relevant failures. A local attacker can use that information to refine privilege-escalation exploits and reconnaissance.

LIN-SYSCTL-BPF.title: Unprivileged eBPF
LIN-SYSCTL-BPF.why: Unprivileged eBPF expands the kernel attack surface available to ordinary users and has historically enabled privilege-escalation vulnerabilities. A compromised account can load BPF programs to probe kernel behavior or exploit verifier and JIT defects.

LIN-SYSCTL-USERNS.title: Unprivileged user namespaces
LIN-SYSCTL-USERNS.semantics: WARN: unprivileged userns creation allowed (unprivileged_userns_clone=1 / max_user_namespaces>0) and not AppArmor-restricted; PASS: disabled or apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1.
LIN-SYSCTL-USERNS.why: Unrestricted user namespaces expose additional kernel namespace and filesystem code to unprivileged processes. Attackers can use that expanded surface to turn kernel vulnerabilities into local privilege escalation, although disabling namespaces can disrupt rootless containers and sandboxing.

fix.label: Disable unprivileged user namespaces where compatible
fix.text: After validating container and application requirements, set kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0 or user.max_user_namespaces=0 in a file under /etc/sysctl.d and apply it with sysctl --system.

LIN-SYSCTL-ASLR.title: ASLR
LIN-SYSCTL-ASLR.why: Incomplete address-space randomization makes process memory locations more predictable. Attackers can use predictable addresses to improve the reliability of memory-corruption exploits and code-reuse attacks.

LIN-SYSCTL-SUIDDUMP.title: setuid core dumps
LIN-SYSCTL-SUIDDUMP.why: Core dumps from set-user-ID or otherwise privileged programs can contain passwords, keys, tokens, and sensitive process memory. An attacker who can access or influence these dumps may recover secrets or overwrite files through unsafe dump handling.

LIN-SYSCTL-PROTLINKS.title: Protected symlinks/hardlinks
LIN-SYSCTL-PROTLINKS.semantics: WARN: fs.protected_symlinks or fs.protected_hardlinks =0; PASS: both 1.
LIN-SYSCTL-PROTLINKS.why: Weak symbolic-link and hard-link protections make shared writable directories more susceptible to link-following attacks. A local attacker can redirect a privileged process toward sensitive files or retain access to files that should no longer be reachable.

LIN-SYSCTL-PERF.title: perf_event paranoia
LIN-SYSCTL-PERF.why: Permissive performance-event access can expose kernel and other-process execution data to unprivileged users. A local attacker can use performance counters for side-channel analysis, reconnaissance, or exploitation of the perf subsystem.

LIN-SYSCTL-IPFWD.title: IPv4 forwarding
LIN-SYSCTL-IPFWD.semantics: WARN: net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 (host routes traffic; pivot aid); PASS: 0.
LIN-SYSCTL-IPFWD.why: IPv4 forwarding allows the host to route traffic between network interfaces. If an attacker compromises the host, that routing capability can support network pivoting or bypass intended segmentation.

fix.label: Retain only for approved routers
fix.text: If the host is intentionally a router, VPN gateway, or container node, document the exception and enforce forwarding paths with a restrictive firewall policy.

LIN-LSM-MAC.title: Mandatory access control
LIN-LSM-MAC.semantics: PASS: SELinux enforcing or AppArmor enabled; WARN: SELinux permissive/disabled and no AppArmor.
LIN-LSM-MAC.why: Without an enforcing mandatory-access-control system, a compromised service is constrained mainly by traditional Unix permissions and discretionary access controls. Attackers can more easily access files, capabilities, and processes available to the compromised account.

fix.label: Enable an enforcing MAC system
fix.text: Enable SELinux in enforcing mode through /etc/selinux/config, or enable AppArmor and load enforcing profiles appropriate to the distribution; test application policy before production rollout.

LIN-FIREWALL.title: Host firewall
LIN-FIREWALL.semantics: PASS: ufw/firewalld/nftables/iptables service active or ufw ENABLED=yes; WARN: none active; ERR: cannot determine.
LIN-FIREWALL.why: Without an active host firewall, every listening service is exposed to any network that can route to the host. Attackers can scan and directly target unnecessary or accidentally exposed services.

test.label: Check common firewall services
test.cmd: systemctl is-active ufw firewalld nftables iptables 2>/dev/null

fix.label: Enable the distribution firewall
fix.text: Configure an allowlist for required management and application traffic, then enable the distribution-supported firewall such as ufw, firewalld, or nftables. Confirm remote-management access before enforcing the policy.

LIN-SSH-ROOTLOGIN.title: SSH root login
LIN-SSH-ROOTLOGIN.semantics: FAIL: PermitRootLogin yes; PASS: no / prohibit-password / forced-commands-only / default; NA: no sshd_config.
LIN-SSH-ROOTLOGIN.why: Direct SSH login as root gives attackers a known privileged username and removes the accountability provided by individual administrator accounts. If root credentials or a root key are compromised, the attacker immediately obtains unrestricted remote access.

fix.label: Disable direct root login
fix.text: Set PermitRootLogin no in /etc/ssh/sshd_config or a validated file under /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d, verify with sshd -t, and reload the SSH service after confirming sudo-capable administrative access.

LIN-SSH-PASSAUTH.title: SSH password authentication
LIN-SSH-PASSAUTH.semantics: WARN: PasswordAuthentication yes (explicit or default); PASS: no; NA: no sshd_config.
LIN-SSH-PASSAUTH.why: SSH password authentication permits online password guessing and exposes reused credentials to credential-stuffing attacks. Disabling it forces stronger key-based or centrally managed authentication when those alternatives are properly protected.

fix.label: Disable SSH password authentication
fix.text: Provision and test public-key or approved centralized authentication, set PasswordAuthentication no in /etc/ssh/sshd_config or a validated drop-in, run sshd -t, and reload the SSH service.

LIN-SSH-EMPTYPW.title: SSH empty passwords
LIN-SSH-EMPTYPW.semantics: FAIL: PermitEmptyPasswords yes; PASS: no/default; NA: no sshd_config.
LIN-SSH-EMPTYPW.why: Permitting empty passwords can allow an account with a blank password to authenticate remotely without knowing a secret. Attackers can enumerate accounts and obtain shell access with trivial authentication.

fix.label: Reject empty passwords over SSH
fix.text: Set PermitEmptyPasswords no in /etc/ssh/sshd_config or a validated drop-in, run sshd -t, and reload the SSH service.

LIN-SSH-X11.title: SSH X11 forwarding
LIN-SSH-X11.semantics: WARN: X11Forwarding yes; PASS: no/default; NA: no sshd_config.
LIN-SSH-X11.why: SSH X11 forwarding extends trust from the server into a client's graphical session and creates additional proxying and authentication-cookie exposure. A compromised server account may use that channel to observe or interact with forwarded X applications.

fix.label: Disable SSH X11 forwarding
fix.text: Set X11Forwarding no in /etc/ssh/sshd_config or a validated drop-in, run sshd -t, and reload the SSH service unless an approved application requires forwarding.

LIN-SSH-MAXAUTH.title: SSH MaxAuthTries
LIN-SSH-MAXAUTH.semantics: WARN: MaxAuthTries >4 (default 6); PASS: <=4; NA: no sshd_config.
LIN-SSH-MAXAUTH.why: A high MaxAuthTries value gives an attacker more authentication attempts within each SSH connection. Reducing it limits online guessing and excessive key offers, although network-level rate limiting remains important.

fix.label: Limit SSH authentication attempts
fix.text: Set MaxAuthTries 4 or lower in /etc/ssh/sshd_config or a validated drop-in, run sshd -t, and reload the SSH service.

LIN-SSH-CIPHERS.title: SSH weak ciphers/MACs/KEX
LIN-SSH-CIPHERS.semantics: WARN: configured Ciphers/MACs/KexAlgorithms include cbc, arcfour, 3des, md5, sha1 KEX or group1; PASS: none configured weak (default set); NA: no sshd_config.
LIN-SSH-CIPHERS.why: Legacy SSH ciphers, MACs, and key-exchange algorithms can provide weaker confidentiality or integrity than modern alternatives. An attacker positioned on the network may exploit cryptographic weaknesses or force use of an unnecessarily weak configured algorithm.

fix.label: Remove legacy SSH algorithms
fix.text: Remove CBC, arcfour, 3DES, MD5, SHA-1 key exchange, and group1 algorithms from Ciphers, MACs, and KexAlgorithms directives; prefer the current OpenSSH defaults, validate with sshd -t, and reload the service.

LIN-SSH-HOSTKEY-PERMS.title: SSH host private key permissions
LIN-SSH-HOSTKEY-PERMS.semantics: FAIL: an /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key is group/world readable or readable by the current non-root user; PASS: otherwise; NA: no host keys.
LIN-SSH-HOSTKEY-PERMS.why: An exposed SSH host private key lets an attacker impersonate the server and can undermine clients that trust that key. Write access can also allow key replacement and persistent interception after the host is restored.

test.label: Inspect host private-key ownership and modes
Find group- or world-readable host private keys

LIN-ACCT-UID0.title: Extra UID 0 accounts
LIN-ACCT-UID0.semantics: FAIL: any account other than root has UID 0; PASS: only root.
LIN-ACCT-UID0.why: Every UID 0 account has the same unrestricted kernel identity as root regardless of its username. An attacker who compromises any additional UID 0 account gains full control while making attribution and account governance harder.

fix.label: Remove unauthorized UID 0 identities
fix.text: Change each non-root UID 0 account to a unique nonzero UID or remove it after reviewing file ownership and service dependencies; retain root as the only UID 0 account.

LIN-ACCT-EMPTYPW.title: Accounts with empty password
LIN-ACCT-EMPTYPW.semantics: FAIL: /etc/shadow has an empty password field; PASS: none; ERR: shadow not readable (needs root).
LIN-ACCT-EMPTYPW.why: An account with an empty password may be accessible without a secret through services or PAM configurations that permit blank passwords. Attackers can target such accounts for immediate local or remote access.

test.label: List accounts with empty password fields

fix.label: Assign credentials where login is required
fix.text: For each reported account, either set a strong managed password through the approved identity process or lock the account if interactive login is unnecessary.

LIN-ACCT-NOPASSWD.title: sudo NOPASSWD rules
LIN-ACCT-NOPASSWD.semantics: WARN: >=1 NOPASSWD rule in sudoers/sudoers.d; PASS: none; ERR: sudoers unreadable (needs root); NA: sudo absent.
LIN-ACCT-NOPASSWD.why: A sudo NOPASSWD rule allows the authorized command to run without a fresh authentication check. Malware or an attacker controlling that account can immediately exercise the delegated privilege, and broad command rules may lead directly to root access.

fix.label: Remove or narrowly scope passwordless sudo
fix.text: Use visudo to remove unnecessary NOPASSWD tags or restrict them to exact non-shell commands with fixed arguments; avoid ALL, interpreters, editors, and commands that can execute arbitrary code.

LIN-ACCT-ADMINS.title: Administrative group members
LIN-ACCT-ADMINS.why: Membership in sudo, wheel, or admin groups identifies accounts that can obtain elevated privileges. An attacker who compromises one of these accounts can often take full control of the host, so the inventory should remain minimal and attributable.

fix.label: Enforce least privilege
fix.text: Review every listed member against current authorization records and remove stale or unnecessary memberships with the distribution's supported account-management process.

LIN-ACCT-UMASK.title: Default umask
LIN-ACCT-UMASK.semantics: WARN: login.defs UMASK grants group/other write (e.g. 002, 000); PASS: 022/027/077.
LIN-ACCT-UMASK.why: A permissive default umask can cause newly created files and directories to be writable by other users. A local attacker may alter shared data, startup files, or scripts created with those unsafe defaults.

fix.label: Set a restrictive default umask
fix.text: Set UMASK 027 in /etc/login.defs, or 077 where users must not share files, and align PAM and shell-profile umask settings so they do not override the policy.

LIN-ACCT-AGING.title: Password maximum age
LIN-ACCT-AGING.semantics: WARN: login.defs PASS_MAX_DAYS unset or >365; PASS: <=365.
LIN-ACCT-AGING.why: Passwords with no maximum age can remain valid indefinitely after silent disclosure or reuse. An attacker who obtains such a password retains a longer opportunity to authenticate unless another control detects and revokes it.

test.label: Read the default maximum password age

fix.label: Set the default maximum age
fix.text: Set PASS_MAX_DAYS to 365 or less in /etc/login.defs and update existing interactive accounts with chage according to the organization's password policy; favor stronger authentication and compromised-password controls where available.

LIN-FILE-SHADOW.title: /etc/shadow permissions
LIN-FILE-SHADOW.semantics: FAIL: /etc/shadow (or gshadow) world-readable or world-writable; PASS: otherwise.
LIN-FILE-SHADOW.why: World-readable shadow files expose password hashes that attackers can crack offline without triggering authentication controls. World-writable shadow or gshadow files can permit account manipulation and direct privilege escalation.

test.label: Find world-readable or world-writable shadow files

fix.label: Restore restricted shadow-file modes
fix.text: Restore the distribution's expected root ownership and shadow-group settings, ensuring neither /etc/shadow nor /etc/gshadow has any permissions for other users; commonly these files use mode 640 or 600.

LIN-FILE-PASSWD.title: /etc/passwd permissions
LIN-FILE-PASSWD.semantics: FAIL: /etc/passwd or /etc/group writable by group/other; PASS: otherwise.
LIN-FILE-PASSWD.why: If /etc/passwd or /etc/group is writable by non-privileged groups or other users, an attacker can manipulate account or group definitions. Such changes can create unauthorized identities, alter privilege relationships, or disrupt authentication.

test.label: Find group- or world-writable account files

LIN-MNT-TMP.title: /tmp mount options
LIN-MNT-TMP.semantics: WARN: /tmp not a separate mount, or mounted without nosuid/nodev; PASS: separate mount with nosuid,nodev.
LIN-MNT-TMP.why: A shared /tmp without a separate mount and nosuid,nodev controls gives temporary files access to the root filesystem's mount behavior. Attackers can abuse device nodes or set-user-ID files where those features are honored, while a separate mount also improves containment of space exhaustion.

test.label: Show the /tmp mount source and options

fix.label: Harden the /tmp mount
fix.text: Create a dedicated /tmp mount or systemd mount unit with nosuid,nodev options, preserve mode 1777 on the directory, and validate application compatibility before adding the persistent configuration to /etc/fstab.

LIN-MNT-SHM.title: /dev/shm mount options
LIN-MNT-SHM.semantics: WARN: /dev/shm mounted without noexec or nosuid; PASS: noexec,nosuid.
LIN-MNT-SHM.why: Allowing executable or set-user-ID content on /dev/shm gives attackers a convenient memory-backed location for payload staging. The noexec and nosuid options reduce common execution and privilege-abuse paths without preventing normal shared-memory use.

fix.label: Harden the shared-memory mount
fix.text: Configure /dev/shm as tmpfs with noexec,nosuid options in /etc/fstab or the applicable systemd mount unit, then remount it during a controlled change after checking application requirements.

LIN-PATH-WW.title: World-writable directories in PATH
LIN-PATH-WW.semantics: FAIL: a directory on PATH (or /etc/environment PATH) is world-writable without sticky bit; PASS: none.
LIN-PATH-WW.why: A non-sticky world-writable directory in PATH lets any local user replace or plant commands that another user may execute by name. Attackers can exploit command search order to run malicious code under an administrator or service account.

test.label: Inspect current PATH directory permissions
test.cmd: printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | while IFS= read -r d; do [ -n "$d" ] || d=.; stat -Lc '%A %a %U:%G %n' -- "$d" 2>/dev/null; done

fix.label: Remove unsafe PATH directories
fix.text: Remove world-writable directories from system and service PATH definitions, or change their ownership and permissions so untrusted users cannot write to them; do not rely on the sticky bit as a substitute for trusted command directories.

LIN-CRON-PERMS.title: Cron configuration permissions
LIN-CRON-PERMS.semantics: FAIL: /etc/crontab or an /etc/cron.* entry is world-writable; PASS: none.
LIN-CRON-PERMS.why: A world-writable system cron file or cron directory entry lets an unprivileged attacker alter commands that a privileged scheduler executes. This can provide reliable persistence and privilege escalation, commonly to root.

fix.label: Remove world-write permission
fix.text: Set root ownership and remove other-user write permission from every reported cron file or directory, using the distribution's package metadata or a known-good peer to confirm the intended mode.

LIN-LOG-AUDITD.title: Audit daemon
LIN-LOG-AUDITD.semantics: PASS: auditd active; WARN: not active.
LIN-LOG-AUDITD.why: Without an active audit daemon, security-sensitive system calls and policy events may not be captured in a durable audit trail. Attackers can operate with less chance that privilege use, account changes, or tampering will be reconstructed.

test.label: Show loaded audit status and rules

fix.label: Enable audit logging
fix.text: Install and enable auditd, configure rules under /etc/audit/rules.d for the host's security requirements, and protect or forward audit logs to limit attacker tampering.

LIN-LOG-SYSLOG.title: System logging
LIN-LOG-SYSLOG.semantics: PASS: rsyslog/syslog-ng active or journald persistent storage; WARN: only volatile journal.
LIN-LOG-SYSLOG.why: A volatile-only journal loses evidence at reboot and may erase the record of an intrusion or crash. Persistent local logging or forwarding through a syslog daemon improves incident reconstruction, although remote protected storage provides stronger resilience.

fix.label: Enable persistent journaling
fix.text: Set Storage=persistent in /etc/systemd/journald.conf or an approved drop-in and ensure /var/log/journal exists with systemd-managed permissions, or enable a supported rsyslog or syslog-ng service.

LIN-TIME-SYNC.title: Time synchronization
LIN-TIME-SYNC.semantics: PASS: chronyd/systemd-timesyncd/ntpd active; WARN: none (breaks Kerberos and log correlation).
